description:
Keeping tens of thousands of safety technology devices active and compliant across a large third-party rental vehicle fleet takes more than day-to-day upkeep, it takes an owner who can see the patterns behind the problems and reshape how the work gets done. You will own device compliance and operational performance for rental vehicles across hundreds of delivery sites, turning device health data into root-cause insight and leading cross-functional partners to durable fixes, not one-off corrections. This role brings that program under a single accountable owner, one person who runs the day-to-day operation and continuously raises the bar on how it performs.
In this role you will own the mechanisms that keep devices installed, accounted for, and active across the rental fleet: the recurring site and partner engagement, the case resolution path, and the operational reporting leaders rely on. You will work across field operations, partner, and support teams to align priorities and drive systemic resolution, delivering difficult cross-functional work independently and escalating when a decision falls outside established mechanisms.
The ideal candidate pairs operational ownership with program-management judgment: the analytical depth to turn recurring issues into root-cause insight, the influence to move multiple stakeholder groups toward a shared outcome without direct authority, and the instinct to simplify and improve the processes they inherit. You will thrive in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment where you own outcomes, not just tasks.
Key job responsibilities
● Own the compliance program for the rental vehicle fleet end to end, keeping devices installed, accounted for, and active across hundreds of sites through the recurring mechanisms you run and improve
● Analyze case and failure trends to identify root causes, then design and implement process improvements that reduce recurring issues rather than resolving them one at a time
● Lead cross-functional stakeholder groups across field operations, partner, and support teams to align priorities, drive systemic resolution, and move compliance and device utilization in the right direction
● Own the operational reporting and device-health analysis that turn raw data into the insight leaders use to make decisions across rental fleet segments
● Identify risks and blockers early, drive crisp and timely decisions, and escalate appropriately to keep the program aligned with its goals
A day in the life
Your day blends operational ownership with cross-functional problem-solving. You will dig into device-health and case data not just to clear what is in front of you but to find the trend underneath it, then bring field operations, partner, and support teams together to fix the root cause. You will design improvements to the mechanisms you own, influence stakeholders toward a shared plan, and build the operational reporting that gives leaders a clear read on program health. Expect to move between focused analysis and the cross-functional work of aligning people and raising the bar across the rental fleet.

We keep the technology devices on Amazon’s last mile and middle mile fleets working, owning device repair, reliability, and availability so vehicles stay on the road. Our group sits at the intersection of field operations, data analysis, and vendor partnership, owning both the daily execution and the strategy behind a healthy device fleet. title: Senior Technical Program Manager, GDCO Central Intelligence and Analytics Team
description:
We're looking for a Senior Technical Product/Program Manager to own a portfolio of these business-facing products and programs end to end: shaping what each one should do and for whom, driving its design and delivery with engineering, science and data technicians, and proving it changes business outcomes. This role is oriented toward business problems and the products/programs that solve them, not toward running shared platform infrastructure. You'll be as comfortable reviewing a system architecture or challenging a recommendations quality as presenting a roadmap to senior executives like VPs.
## The portfolio you'll own
- **Self-service analytics, to production.** Take our natural-language and SQL analytics product over the governed data lake from team tool to a production service leaders rely on: accuracy on governed metrics, onboarding new domains, reliability, access controls, and adoption.
- **Recommendation engine delivery and quality.** Deliver the AI-assisted recommendation engine from pilot to broad use, own its quality bar: what it recommends, with what confidence, when it should stay silent, and how we know it worked.
- **Business domain decision products.** Our operation runs on a few core business domains, each with its own leaders, metrics, data sources, and decisions. For each one, you'll own the product that moves a leader from "what's happening" to "what should I do about it": define the decisions it supports, the metrics and data it needs, and how we measure whether it improved the domain's outcome. Today that means: data products that cover repair backlog and aging, repair throughput and turnaround time, parts availability and other blockers, and repeat failures. The core decision is where to focus the effort so it returns the most capacity to customers fastest. Data products track deliveries from plan through install and hand-off, show what's on track, what's at risk, and why (parts, labor, facilities, network readiness), and route each blocker to the owner who can clear it. The core decision is which at-risk deliveries need intervention now. Success is more capacity delivered on its committed date.
Key job responsibilities
- **Own program strategy and roadmap** for each product/program in the portfolio, tied to a business outcome (repair turnaround, labor productivity, capacity on time), and phase scope deliberately from pilot to GA.
- **Define and enforce quality.** Set the bar for each products/programs, such as answer accuracy for self-service analytics or recommendation precision, confidence, and abstain behavior for the recommendation engine. Partner with engineering and science so no product presents correlation as causation or claims more confidence than it has earned.
- **Prove business impact.** Define how actions are captured, how impact is measured against matched baselines, and how outcomes feed back into the product. Success is not "recommendations accepted" or "queries run"; it's decisions that changed outcomes.
- **Run technical delivery with the engineering team.** Own the delivery cadence, sprint planning, and release management for your products/programs. Review design docs, understand the architecture well enough to weigh tradeoffs (build vs. reuse, latency vs. cost, coupling between services), and keep scope, sequencing, and dependencies honest.
- **Drive launch readiness** across security review, penetration testing, operational readiness (ORR), and privacy reviews for each product moving to production.
- **Lead cross-org dependencies** with Supply Chain, Hardware Engineering, Facilities, workforce planning, and peer data teams: write the asks, negotiate data contracts, and escalate when a partner dependency blocks the roadmap.
- **Write the narratives** (PR/FAQs, 6-pagers, pilot readouts) for Director and VP audiences, with honest accounting of what is proven vs. pending.

Our team is focused on building and delivering data solutions that drive meaningful outcomes for AWS and our customers. We operate in a collaborative environment where program managers work closely with engineers, scientists, and business leaders to tackle challenging problems at scale. title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, GES NA, Technical Vendor Management, Design and Construction
description:
Are you an innovative leader that wants to lead the cross-functional design and deployment of innovative solutions into our world-class existing fulfillment centers and logistics systems? Do you want to take ownership of solving the industry’s most complex problems? Does the challenge of designing and implementing ground breaking solutions for automated material handling equipment, packaging technologies, and systems including robotics and high-speed manufacturing appeal to you? If you’re looking to be challenged in a fast paced and often ambiguous environment, and you have strong technical problem solving and project management skills, then this job is for you!
Amazon is searching for an innovative and solutions-oriented Technical Program Manager who is able to collaborate effectively with internal and external technical teams and be responsible for the design, development and deployment of our material handling systems across multiple building types. The role primarily focuses on the Technical Program Management of integrating systems and devices and delivering turnkey deployable solutions to be delivered in the field.
In this role you will be responsible for working with internal customers to define highly ambiguous problem statements, influencing a global Amazon MHE sourcing and integration strategy, writing technical specifications and performing technical evaluations on equipment, generating multiyear budgets, driving project schedules from design to release, and managing multiple large, high visibility programs simultaneously through the project lifecycle.
This person will possess a strong engineering and program management background, will have demonstrated experience leading medium to large projects, and will have a well-rounded technical background in current MHE technologies and storage solutions. You must be able to thrive and succeed in an innovative environment, and not be hindered by ambiguity or competing priorities. This means you are not only able to develop and drive high-level strategic initiatives, but can also roll up your sleeves, dig in, and get the job done.
This role requires 50% regional travel and availability to work from a corporate office when not traveling. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of the office. Relocation assistance may be provided.
Key job responsibilities
- Own multiple large, complex programs through the full development and deployment lifecycle — you are the accountable driver from concept through field delivery
- Partner with internal customers to define ambiguous problem statements and translate them into clear technical requirements and specifications
- Contribute to Amazon's MHE sourcing and integration strategy by evaluating vendor capabilities, performing technical assessments, and generating data-driven recommendations
- Understand product integration requirements across mechanical, electrical, and controls functions at a systems level
- Critique and debate technical designs, assess viability of proposed solutions, and help engineering teams make appropriate trade-offs considering business goals, throughput, quality, maintainability, and operability
- Drive project schedules from design through release, managing dependencies and risks across internal and external stakeholders
- Generate multiyear budgets and track program financials
- Identify engineering standards and drive consistent application of changes across North America
- Synthesize complex technical and business inputs into clear documentation and specifications
- Lead weekly Team Leads Sync meetings — facilitate agenda, surface hot topics, and track open action items
- Facilitate bi-weekly Team All Call meetings, coordinating topic shares across the team
- Compile and distribute bi-weekly Lookahead/Flash reports covering highlights, lowlights, key meetings, FAT testing schedules, and vendor POCs
- Manage monthly document reviews, ensuring working papers are reviewed internally before leadership submission
- Support quarterly business reviews by compiling executive summaries, sub-pillar updates, FAQs, and appendices
- Prepare quarterly Big Rocks updates for leadership review
- Coordinate annual Charter/Strategy and Headcount Reviews, maintaining documentation in SharePoint and WorkDocs
- Support annual goal-setting processes and provide monthly goal update reminders
- Manage the Team Request Tracker — assign and track action items across team members
- Maintain and optimize operational mechanisms in Smartsheet and Slack to support team workflows
A day in the life
Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Technical Vendor Management operates at the intersection of engineering execution and vendor partnership across North America. A day in the life may involve leading a weekly business review with a general contractor, reviewing scorecard data to identify systemic performance patterns, conducting a strategic planning session with your team leads, or presenting portfolio risk assessments to GES leadership. You will engage with vendor executives, coordinate with GPO on sourcing decisions, align with TVM counterparts, and drive cross-portfolio intelligence that no single project team can see. GES NA Technical Vendor Management is highly collaborative, working daily to make vendor performance consequential, vendor relationships strategic, and Amazon’s construction supply base stronger every year.
About the team
The Technical Vendor Management (TVM) organization is an engineering and performance-focused function within NA GES, consisting of five pillars: TVM MHE Vendor Management, TVM MHE Vendor Development, TVM MHE Components, Construction Contracts, and Technical Vendor Management, Construction. We manage the full project lifecycle of Amazon’s vendor relationships for general contractors and specialty subcontractors—from qualification through active project execution, performance accountability, and continuous improvement. Technical Vendor Management exists because vendor performance directly impacts whether Amazon’s network launches on time, on budget, and at the quality level operations require. With our team, vendor performance improves year over year because we make it consequential. We build strategic relationships that unlock decisions site-level teams cannot reach, see patterns across the portfolio that no single project can see, and act on them before they repeat.

title: Technical Program Manager III - Edge Connectivity Services, Edge Connectivity
description:

You will also work with Defense Industrial Base (DIB) customers to support and expand Amazon's new launched AWS Secret Cloud for Industry (ASCI) service which enables dedicated connectivity to the AWS Secret Region for industry partners. You will build mechanisms and processes to automate and streamline the customer experience, working across AWS engineering, networking, and security teams to simplify access to the AWS classified (Secret and Top Secret) regions.
Are you energized by solving complex technical challenges that span multiple teams and systems? Do you thrive when turning ambiguity into clear plans and measurable outcomes? In this role, you will define program strategy, align stakeholders across engineering and business teams, and deliver results at scale. You will use your technical depth to question assumptions, assess architectural decisions, and ensure the right solutions ship on time. Key job responsibilities
- Define and manage the lifecycle of complex cross-functional programs, setting clear objectives, success criteria, and roadmaps that align with organizational goals.
- Drive alignment across business and technical stakeholders by facilitating crisp decision-making, providing context for technology choices, and prioritizing initiatives based on customer and business impact.
- Identify and mitigate risks proactively by overseeing gaps between teams, processes, and system architectures, reducing exposure to common failure modes such as unclear requirements or insufficient testing.
- Leverage your technical judgment to evaluate proposals, test assumptions, and make smart trade-offs between time, effort, and feature scope while partnering with engineering leaders to ensure solutions scale appropriately.
- Communicate program progress and outcomes effectively through written narratives and executive presentations, building consensus when perspectives differ and escalating with good judgment when needed.
- Partner with Business, Product, and Technology Leaders and teams to deliver value for our customers
- Drive visibility and transparency of dates, milestones, and schedule throughout the customer onboarding process
- Build inclusive relationships with partner groups in AWS Region Services, Networking and the World Wide Public Sector teams. Ensuring that these teams focus on our customers and support customer missions.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing program metrics and identifying areas that need attention before joining a cross-team sync to unblock a critical dependency. By midafternoon, you could be drafting a narrative that frames a key trade-off for senior leadership, then pivoting to a design review where you pressure-test architectural assumptions with engineers. You will regularly connect with stakeholders across the organization, ensuring priorities stay aligned and your program delivers meaningful results.
About the team
Our team is focused on building and improving the technology systems that power Amazon's operations at global scale. We value collaboration, clear communication, and a willingness to tackle hard problems together. You will work alongside engineers, product managers, and business leaders who are committed to delivering impactful solutions for our customers. We are investing in new capabilities and looking for a program leader who is excited to help shape our technical direction in the years ahead.

- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Current, active TS/SCI US Government Security Clearance

- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Technical Program Manager, Amazon Key
description:
Amazon Key for Business (KfB) builds the technology that lets Amazon delivery associates and partners securely access multi-family buildings, gated communities, and commercial properties. Our systems power millions of secure deliveries by connecting Amazon's logistics network with building access hardware, property management platforms, and third-party smart locks around the world.
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive cross-functional programs across our engineering, product, business development, and operations partners. You will own program execution end to end: defining scope with stakeholders, building the plan, identifying dependencies and risks early, and keeping a distributed set of engineering teams aligned on delivery. You will work on programs such as access hardware integrations, third-party lock partnerships, technician installation tooling, and access-security initiatives, in close partnership with product and engineering leaders.
This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys turning ambiguity into a clear plan, is comfortable reading a design document and asking the right technical questions, and communicates crisply with audiences ranging from engineers to senior leadership.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end execution of cross-team technical programs, from requirements definition through launch and post-launch operations.
- Partner with engineering managers and senior engineers to translate business requirements into technical scope, milestones, and delivery plans.
- Identify dependencies, risks, and critical path items early; drive mitigation and escalate with clear options and recommendations.
- Coordinate across engineering teams in multiple time zones, as well as product, business development, operations, security, and external partners.
- Run program reviews and write clear, concise status updates, decision documents, and launch readiness assessments for leadership.
- Establish and improve mechanisms for intake, prioritization, and release coordination so the team can deliver predictably as program volume grows.
- Measure program outcomes against goals and drive continuous improvement in how the team plans and delivers.
A day in the life
You might start the day reviewing overnight progress from engineering teams in Europe and Asia, then run a working session with product and engineering to close open questions on a new partner integration. In the afternoon you update the program plan after a dependency shifted, write a short status note to leadership with the impact and your recommendation, and prepare for a launch readiness review later in the week.
About the team
The KfB engineering organization is a globally distributed team of software development engineers, systems development engineers, and technical program managers across North America, Europe, and Asia. We own the backend services, device integrations, mobile applications, and internal tooling behind Amazon Key for Business. We value ownership, bias for action, and direct, respectful communication, and we are investing heavily in AI-assisted development to move faster.

Imagine building AI infrastructure at Apple — systems that power how products are made, how engineers think, and ultimately how hundreds of millions of people experience technology every day.
Here is your opportunity to join an engineering team moving Apple's algorithms programs into the AI era. We are developing AI systems that enhance the way engineers work by incorporating human judgment and integrating with data and tools. Our aim is to seamlessly incorporate AI into our processes.
We are looking for a software engineer who thrives at the intersection of data systems, AI tooling, and developer experience. You'll design and build platforms that connect AI to the deep organizational context it needs to be genuinely useful — and put those capabilities directly into the hands of the engineers shipping Apple's next-generation sensing technologies. Some of what you build will power internal workflows; some may evolve into products and tools that reach far beyond our team.
You will work alongside machine learning scientists, algorithm engineers, hardware teams, designers, and human factors researchers to build the AI-native platforms and data systems that accelerate how Apple ships its next generation of devices. We're a small, high-impact group with an ambitious roadmap — you'll have outsized influence on the architecture and direction of what we build.
The algorithms behind Apple's most beloved features span software, hardware, and design — and the AI infrastructure you build will serve all of them. You'll be at the center of a uniquely cross-functional environment where world-class talent in each discipline depends on the platforms you create to move faster and make better decisions. The best ideas here have a way of starting as internal tools and growing into something bigger — you'll help shape that trajectory.
You might have built a chatbot that needed to reason over internal docs, designed an agent that orchestrated multi-step tool calls, or created a pipeline that turned unstructured data into searchable knowledge. What matters is that you've gone beyond tutorials — you've shipped AI-powered tools that real users depend on.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or related degree
3+ years of s relevant industry expeience
Proficiency in Python and at least one of: Swift, TypeScript, or another systems-level language
Experience designing and building backend services, data pipelines, or platform infrastructure
Hands-on experience building with modern AI/agent frameworks
Strong software architecture and API design sensibilities — you think in systems, not scripts
Experience building retrieval pipelines (RAG, embeddings, vector search) or knowledge retrieval systems
Strong communicator who works effectively across disciplines
Experience evaluating and iterating on AI system outputs — you've built evaluation pipelines, measured quality, and know that shipping AI means shipping feedback loops
Sharp problem-solving instincts and a bias toward shipping
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD n Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or related degree
Experience building macOS or iOS client applications
Background in workflow orchestration, experiment tracking, or reproducibility tooling
Experience designing data models, storage layers, or integration APIs for complex domains
Experience integrating LLMs with external tools and APIs (tool-use patterns, MCP, function calling) or building custom integrations between LLMs and external systems
Familiarity with access-controlled or policy-aware data systems
Experience with vector databases or embedding pipelines (Pinecone, Chroma, pgvector, or similar)
Track record building developer tools, CLIs, or internal platforms that engineers rely on daily
Experience with cloud AI services (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI) or self-hosted model serving
Contributions to open-source projects in AI/ML infrastructure
Comfort navigating large, established codebases and shipping iteratively within them

title: Applied AI Engineer - Health
description:
The Health Personalization team builds AI-driven health experiences that provide our users with understandable, actionable information about their health and wellbeing. We harness large language models and the latest ML advances to build products that are useful, personal, privacy-preserving, and safe — turning research and incubation into features people rely on every day. As part of the larger Sensor Software & Prototyping team, we work across hardware platforms and data modalities including wearables and natural language input. We are committed to building deeply personal features that understand, anticipate, and adapt to users' behaviors and uphold Apple's deep commitment to privacy as a fundamental human right. Our team values expertise, innovation, and inclusivity. Come join us!
In this role, you will prototype, develop, evaluate, and ship Generative AI experiences for real-world health and wellbeing applications. You'll apply strong ML fundamentals, build practical evaluation methods, and ground your work in real on-device user interactions. Your work will directly shape customer-facing health products across the full ML lifecycle.
A strong candidate makes progress through ambiguity — building, learning from real data, and iterating toward the right answer rather than waiting for the perfect plan. They take ownership of outcomes end-to-end, prioritize well, and learn fast.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years relevant industry experience
Ability to leverage AI-assisted tooling to write clean, performant code (e.g. Python), while maintaining full ownership of code quality and software development best practices (e.g. Git).
Technical expertise and hands-on experience building and evaluating machine learning solutions for user-facing applications.
Comfort building functional prototypes or proof-of-concept demos to test ideas quickly.
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD in computer science, machine learning, health informatics, biomedical engineering, or a related quantitative field — or equivalent industry experience.
Strong communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Technical expertise in generative AI domains, such as large language model architectures, knowledge retrieval, and natural language understanding.
Deep expertise with LLM-based evaluation systems and evidence-based approaches to test development and quality measurement.
Customer-focused mindset with experience or strong interest in building consumer digital health and wellness products.
Experience building and deploying performant on-device or full-stack systems, including rapid prototyping of user-facing experiences (e.g. Swift, SwiftUI), is a plus.

title: Broadcast Engineer
description:
We want the World to be a better place! Join our team and imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.
Apple's worldwide events team informs the world about our innovative products and services and the values that drive our company. The team produces some of the most technically demanding and widely watched live productions in the world. As a broadcast engineer you'll sit at the center of it all, keeping the infrastructure that makes these moments possible running.
We're seeking a hands-on broadcast engineer to work across permanent facilities and temporary event environments. You'll work at the intersection of traditional broadcast engineering and modern IP media systems, helping ensure the technical systems that carry video, audio, and data from source to screen are ready, reliable, and resilient when it matters most. Your work is directly visible, in the clarity of a signal path during a live keynote, in the run-book that guides a team through a flawless remote production, and in the infrastructure decisions that shape how Apple communicates at scale
This role provides hands-on engineering support for broadcast facilities, transmission operation centers, and event production environments. You will work across live production, infrastructure readiness, signal routing, media transport, encoding, monitoring, and troubleshooting, with a strong focus on IP-based media workflows.
You will partner with production, engineering, infosec, operations, vendors, and cross-functional teams to plan, deploy, operate, and maintain systems that support high-visibility events. This role requires sound technical judgment, clear communication, and the ability to stay focused under live production conditions. You should be comfortable moving between rack-level work, system configuration, documentation, real-time troubleshooting, and longer-term infrastructure improvement.
Minimum qualifications: 4+ years of hands-on broadcast engineering experience in live events, broadcast facilities, production operations, or similarly demanding media environments.
Direct experience operating or supporting one or more broadcast platforms such as Imagine, Evertz, TAG, Providius, EVS, AWS Elemental, Ateme, Appear, or Nimbra.
Working knowledge of IP media transport technologies, including SMPTE ST 2110, NMOS IS-04/05, JPEG-XS, SRT, AES67 and Dante.
An understanding of IP networking in a broadcast context, including multicast, PTP/IEEE 1588, VLANs, QoS, IGMP.
Hands-on experience with network infrastructure in a broadcast, media, or production environment.
You are comfortable administering, troubleshooting, and supporting Linux and macOS systems used in broadcast operations.
You can diagnose signal, network, timing, and system issues under live production conditions.
You communicate clearly with production, engineering, operations, and vendor teams, especially when priorities change or issues arise in real time.
You use sound judgment to balance technical risk, production impact, and operational continuity.
You are able to travel approximately 20% for remote event support.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with cloud media services or hybrid workflows, including AWS MediaConnect or related platforms.
Familiarity with VMware virtualization supporting broadcast or media applications.
Background supporting corporate events, technology-sector events, product launches, town halls, or executive communications.
Experience contributing to technical operations center buildouts, facility upgrades, or infrastructure migrations.
Scripting or automation experience with Python, Bash, or similar tools applied to broadcast infrastructure.
Familiarity with professional broadcast communications systems, including intercom, IFB, and program audio distribution.
Experience with Arista network infrastructure in a broadcast, media or production environment.

title: Camera Architect
description:

The camera architecture team initiates and fosters deep collaboration between all cross functional teams involved to deliver final camera performance and features, from the hardware level to user facing applications. The end goal is to successfully tie in highly optimized camera hardware solutions with state-of-the-art software providing market leading imaging experiences.
The ideal candidate is someone who can perform detailed system analysis and tradeoff evaluations, derive camera and camera system requirements from use cases, and characterize and simulate optical systems to aid the design and validation process.
As a Camera Architect you will be working closely with camera HW, product HW, algorithm and SW teams on future Apple imaging solutions.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Imaging Science or equivalent and a minimum 3 years of relevant experience.
Familiarity with camera technologies and optical science, knowledge in two or more of the following areas: optics, camera calibration, computer vision, image quality metrics, image sensor and pixel fundamentals, image processing pipeline
Preferred qualifications: MS, or PhD in Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Imaging Science or equivalent
Experience in three of the follow camera technologies and optical science areas: optics, camera calibration, computer vision, image quality metrics, image sensor and pixel fundamentals, image processing pipeline
Experience defining camera metrics and specifications through product goals, user studies and image/data analysis
Understanding of important camera metrics and common design tradeoffs to achieve required goals
Ability to communicate and collaborate with cross-functional partners to recommend solutions and influence product decisions at leadership level

Strong understanding and hands-on experience with 3A’s, denoising, sharpening, fusion, and tone-mapping algorithms.
Technical familiarity with machine learning and image processing technologies.
Excellent photography, videography, and cinematography skills.
Proficiency in at least one of the following: C, C++, Objective-C, Swift, Python, or shell programming.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with experience in cross-functional collaboration.
Bachelor’s Degree in Imaging Science, Imaging Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Color Science, or a related field.

Experience with software and hardware on consumer devices and cell phone cameras.
Experience with iOS/macOS app development.
Knowledge or research experience in human vision and psychophysics.

description:
Join the Wireless Technologies and Ecosystems (WTE) organization and be part of a best-in-class team of engineers, working with multi-functional teams to drive innovation and develop products used by millions worldwide. We are looking for a highly reciprocal individual who can excel in a high-paced environment. Be ready to make something extraordinary when you come here. title: Design Verification Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet and changing the game? We have an opportunity for an outstandingly hardworking design verification engineer! As a member of our wide-ranging group, you will have the rare and extraordinary opportunity to craft upcoming products that will delight and encourage millions of Apple’s customers daily.
This role is for a DV engineer who will enable us to produce fully functional first silicon for IP designs. The responsibilities include all phases of pre-silicon verification including but not limited to: establishing DV methodology, test-plan development, verification environment development including stimulus and checkers, test-writing, debug, coverage, sign-off for RTL freeze and tape-out.
In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring bug-free first silicon for part of the SoC / IP and are encouraged to develop detailed test and coverage plans based on the micro-architecture. You are responsible for developing verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring a scalable and portable environment. You will get to develop verification environment, including all the respective components such as stimulus, checkers, assertions, trackers, coverage. A mindset to break the design is highly desirable.
Furthermore, you will develop verification plans for all features under your care, execute verification plans, including design bring-up, DV environment bring- up, regression enabling features, and debug of the test failures. You will also learn to develop block, IP and SoC level test-benches track and report DV progress using a variety of metrics, including bugs and coverage. You will also be expected to make use of LLM and related technologies to achieve efficient execution and improved quality.
Minimum qualifications: BS degree in technical subject area and a minimum 3 years relevant industry experience or equivalent.
Preferred qualifications: MS degree in a technical subject area and relevant industry experience strongly preferred
Strong knowledge of OOP, SystemVerilog and UVM
Strong knowledge in developing scalable and portable testbenches
Proven experience with verification methodologies and tools such as simulators, waveform viewer, build and run automation, coverage collection, and gate-level simulations
Working experience using LLMs for efficiency and quality
Experience with power-aware (UPF) or similar verification methodology
Knowledge of one of the scripting languages such as Python, Perl, TCL
Some experience with serial protocols such as PCIe or USB, parallel protocol such as DDR is a plus but not required
Knowledge of formal verification methodology is a plus but not required

title: Digital Mixed Signal Design and Modeling Engineer
description:
Join our team at Apple developing complex mixed-signal IPs for Apple’s custom integrated circuits. Our team has shipped hundreds of millions of chips into Apple’s existing product lines, and is developing new chips for future product lines!

Solid fundamentals in digital design and RTL development (SystemVerilog/Verilog).
Good knowledge of analog circuits and architectures (e.g., power converters, regulators, references, ADCs/DACs).
Experience with industry-standard simulation and verification tools (e.g., Xcelium, Virtuoso).
Strong debugging and cross-functional communication skills.

title: SoC Power Spec Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for crafting new solutions? As part of our Silicon Engineering group, you will generate ideas and turn them into reality. You will be part of the team responsible for crafting state-of-the-art ASICs that are integral to many Apple products. We are looking for an engineer who will work on the modeling of power dissipation of various IPs and applications, including AI/ML and power modeling at the SOC/system level for Apple products. This role provides an opportunity to participate in optimization of a variety of leading edge chips for power-efficiency. You will collaborate across many teams including architecture, SOC design, and system design. The job also involves partnering with the lab and silicon characterization/validation teams on correlating the models to the silicon data.
The job involves collaborating across many fields and playing a role of getting innovative products to millions of customers. You will have the opportunity to build new insights into silicon optimization, as well as work with architects, silicon design engineers, software developers, and be involved in silicon/model correlation efforts of mobile SoC design.
Your main responsibilities will be:
-Modeling power dissipation at the SOC level, including Neural Engines, CPUs, Graphics, compute ( AI/ML) accelerators, media IPs, caches and fabric.
-Modeling power dissipation for customer use-cases.
-Interacting with the System designers, Technology team, Silicon Validation, and Product Engineering teams to define power targets at the SOC level, and the power delivery.
-Working with the power lab and test teams to correlate models to silicon data.
Minimum qualifications: A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience.
Preferred qualifications: We would prefer our SoC Power Spec Engineer to have the following qualifications:
MSEE preferred
Deep knowledge of SOC architecture and power modeling.
Deep understanding of SOC building blocks including CPU, GPU, caches, memory and media IPs
Skills in scripting and data analysis.
Understanding of VLSI design flow and CMOS technology and background in EE.
Ability to understand and model thermal control loops and throttling mechanisms.
Strong teammate with excellent communication skills.

title: Wireless Module Engineer
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other’s ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It’s the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something. The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is well-versed in multiple fields for wireless module development: RF design, packaging, product engineering (including yield analysis), ATE, and reliability engineering.
The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is a highly motivated, self-driven technical lead responsible for driving the development of wireless modules from early architecture definition through mass-production ramp. This role requires strong cross-functional collaboration and the ability to deeply engage across a broad spectrum of technical domains including RF design, reliability, manufacturing test, supply chain, and system integration. The WME will initiate and lead early-phase RF architecture and specification discussions between internal engineering teams and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly & Test (OSAT). They will ensure all OSATs comply with internal specification formats, review procedures, and approval workflows. The WME will drive the formal module design release process, establishing and reviewing checkpoints for schematics, PCB layout, electromagnetic/RF simulation results, design-for-manufacturability (DFM), test data readiness, and OSAT design feedback
In addition to communicating risks and priorities, the core responsibility of WME is to manage module integration and ATE test coverage at OSATs. WME will function as a general manager overseeing all aspects of ATE maturity preparation for hardware—such as load boards, daughter cards, sockets, and handlers—and software, firmware, module calibrations, GRR, and CPK/data analysis.
This role is expected to drive OSATs, set priorities, and collaborate closely with them to validate and approve the final ATE hardware and software integration, test coverage, and corresponding test limits, ensuring timely delivery of tested modules for product NPI builds. Following the NPI builds, WME will lead the failure analysis process with the OSATs and work with them to implement improvement activities, including enhancing ATE testers, optimizing software/firmware test time, and improving overall yield and retest rates. This role will involve traveling to international OSATs for Module & ATE bring up for 1-2 weeks before the product NPI builds. WME is expected to have a broad spectrum of technical depth to debug additional bring up issues during travel. For e.g. I2C & PCIe interface related issues. This team member will facilitate collaboration with multi-functional groups at Apple and define the test coverage. Typical test coverage includes but not limited to Open-Short & Continuity test, VCO calibration and test, TX/RX power calibration and test, RF packet test, EVM test, RX sensitivity test. They will collaborate closely with internal reliability engineering teams to translate expected product field-usage profiles into feasible and data-driven reliability test models for modules and components. This role supports multiple product lines within the Hardware Technology organization, ensuring technical excellence, risk visibility, and disciplined execution from early concept through manufacturing ramp.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 10 years relevant industry experience
Strong RF fundamentals.
Proven track record for effective written/verbal communication, leading projects with self-motivation.
Preferred qualifications: 2 or more years of wireless module development experience from early concept to MP for consumer electronic devices.
Strong RF design background. Additional experience in packaging, product engineering, ATE, and reliability engineering is highly desirable.
Strong data analysis skills including yield analysis (Cpk), and retest rate analysis, required for data sheet closures.
Capable of working at both high-level theory and detailed hands-on execution.
Experienced in managing vendor teams and leading cross-time-zone meetings.
AI/ML experience with expertise in Data Analysis is a plus.

title: iOS Engineer - Wallet
description:
The Wallet Engineering team is looking for proactive and hardworking software engineers to join our growing team! Wallet allows you to securely collect and use boarding passes, movie tickets, coupons, and more, all in one place. It’s also the home for Apple Pay, the easiest and most convenient way to pay in stores, apps, and on the web.
Beyond payments, the Wallet Engineering team is building the technology to replace the physical wallet. We have been hard at work, creating groundbreaking experiences with Apple Card, Apple Cash, and Apple Savings, and we’ve revolutionized how our customers ride public transit in cities around the world, including London, New York, and Tokyo. Join us and work on an exciting roadmap of features that change the everyday lives of people around the world.
The Transit, Access, Identity, and Provisioning team (San Diego / Cupertino): The team is responsible for all user-facing features, such as buying transit cards in Wallet, viewing balances and commute plans, as well as NFC Express mode, which allows you to travel securely and privately on transit without needing to FaceID every time. Access expanded on this platform created by Transit to introduce hotel and home keys, car keys, student ID, and Disney MagicMobile. Access introduced Passive Entry, which allows transactions similar to NFC Express mode but over UWB and so occur at range, making the car key experience feel just the same as the key fob. Identity completed this platform journey by allowing driver’s licenses, government ID’s, and other documents into Wallet. Finally, underpinning all of Wallet products is provisioning. The infrastructure, user experience, and process of adding any card to Wallet. This team supports all Wallet requests across the organization to ensure a unified experience.
The First Party Products team (Cupertino / New York): Responsible for Apple Card, Apple Savings, Apple Cash, Gift Cards, Issuer Installments, and Tap to Pay.  - Lead new hardware bring-up end to end, from peripheral configuration and driver development through BSP/HAL integration, and cut the time it takes to get new boards running.

 - Implement and tune deterministic real-time control and protection on multi-core MCUs, partitioning work across cores and staying within hard ISR timing and jitter budgets.

 - Build reusable firmware libraries and coding standards in place of product-specific implementations, so each new product ships faster than the last.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Hands-on experience shipping bare-metal and/or RTOS firmware on modern microcontrollers (e.g. ARM Cortex-M), including taking one or more products to manufacturing.

 - Deep expertise in C/C++: clean, modular, defensive code, with a solid grasp of memory management, ISR-safe patterns, and compiler and runtime behavior.

 - Comfort reading schematics and datasheets and working directly with hardware and power electronics engineers to make sound design and processor-selection tradeoffs.

 - Strong instincts for firmware architecture: clean separation of responsibilities, minimal shared state, observability built in from the start, and designs that roll out safely and fail predictably.

 - Nice to have: experience designing deterministic real-time control and protection on multi-core MCUs, with robust fault handling and safe recovery.

Cox Fleet keeps your fleet moving!
Headquartered in Indianapolis, Cox Fleet has grown to become one of the largest fleet maintenance companies in the country.
Cox Fleet is the leading provider of on-site mobile maintenance and repair services nationwide, offering mobile on-site fleet service for light medium, and heavy-duty trucks and trailers. Cox Fleet also services customers utilizing its 50+ nationwide service centers; each offering accident repair, painting, refurbishment, and heavy mechanical repair. We are supported by a 24/7 in-house call-center and provide scheduled maintenance services and unscheduled services to fleets anywhere, anytime.
Cox Fleet is currently hiring a  Mobile Diesel Technician Level 2 or Sr Mobile Diesel Mechanic (Level 3)
The Mobile Diesel Technician Level II will be responsible for performing licensed DOT inspections, Preventative Maintenance inspections, light and follow-up repairs, light mechanical/hydraulic/electrical and electronic diagnostics, and other duties as assigned.  The Mobile Diesel Technician II can perform more advanced diagnostics and repairs under the supervision of a Sr Mobile Diesel Technician or higher. The Diesel Technician II continues to learn additional advanced mechanical skills and diagnostic techniques.  A successful Diesel Technician II complies with all company policies and achieves high level performance metrics.
DUTIES:
Perform scheduled preventative maintenance (“PM”), DOT Inspections and follow up repairs on light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles in a mobile/field environment.
Perform minor adjustment and repairs on various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Diagnose, adjust, and repair various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Air conditioning systems, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Inspect, test, and listen to defective equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using test instruments such as handheld computers and pressure gauges.
Road test vehicles to diagnose malfunctions and to ensure that they are working properly.
Identify problems, determine accuracy and relevance of information, using sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives.
Independently manage parts inventory and equipment provided on company-issued service truck and perform periodic reconciliation.
Maintain and operate company-issued service vehicle, conduct safety checks, and pre-/post-trip inspections of vehicle.
Work with and listen effectively to clients and customers to assess their needs, providing information or assistance, resolving their problems, or satisfying their expectations.
Manage concurrent assigned tasks, making effective judgments as to prioritizing work related activities and time allocations.
Use hand tools, precision instruments, as well as Diesel tools, welding equipment, lift and jacks.
Document according to company standards and upload pictures of work performed, parts used, and all findings observed on Repair Orders (“RO”) using company-issued iOS device and our proprietary TRAIT application.
Accurately complete DOT forms and all other forms of documentation in a timely fashion.
Work with a high degree of independence and manage own daily schedule.
Maintain a high level of productivity and be able to work within or close to most Standard Repair Times.
Obtain parts from approved local and national vendors as necessary for the repairs to be performed.
Communicate with management and support team via email or phone to obtain approvals on repair estimates, retrieve purchase order numbers and/or discuss RO findings notes.
Perform all work in compliance with organizational safety, health and environmental policies, and federal regulations, to include OSHA, EPA, and DOT.
Maintain company issued service truck, conduct safety checks and daily pre/post trip inspections.
REQUIREMENTS:
High School Diploma/GED and 3 years’ experience in a related field. The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as any level degree/certification beyond a HS diploma/GED in a related discipline; or 5 years’ experience in a related field.
Possess and supply a set of hand tools necessary to perform required job duties.
Obtain Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) certification T8 (PMI) within eighteen (18) months.
This position follows regulations issued by the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). Candidate must be able to successfully complete and pass a DOT-regulated pre-employment background screening and DOT physical prior to employment.

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. The AML & EDD Financial Crime Review Analyst is responsible for performing transaction activity reviews, investigations and customer due diligence reviews on customers that have been alerted for potentially suspicious activity, potential sanctions list matches or that have been identified as posing elevated risk for money laundering and terrorist financing. They will be responsible for ensuring that reviews and investigations are maintained at a level commensurate with regulatory expectations. This role will assist in Suspicious Activity Reporting (SAR), and/or enhanced due diligence (EDD) reviews on customers identified as posing a higher inherent risk and/or sanctions screening.
Primary Responsibilities:
Reviewing and investigating alerts, performing investigations, or enhanced due diligence reviews for potentially suspicious activity, making risk-based SAR recommendations and preparing SARs.
Conducting periodic holistic reviews of higher risk individuals or entities.
Reviewing and investigating potential matches with sanctions lists.
Maintaining a solid working knowledge (functional and operational) of the rules and regulations, including but not limited to, BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC and Sanctions Screening.
Assist in the delivery of financial crime consulting services to Financial Services companies, including Banks, Money Service Businesses (MSB’s), Third Party Payment Providers, and FinTechs.
Handle other duties as assigned.

High School Diploma.
1-year minimum experience in financial services Financial Crime compliance management, retail banking, commercial banking, and/or global diversified financial services organizations.
Knowledge of the laws applicable to money laundering, to include the BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC requirements and Suspicious Activity Reporting requirements.
Strong writing, analytical, and communication skills and the ability to multi-task and complete projects on time.
Strong research skills and sound knowledge in the use of the Microsoft Office Suite and experience with on-line research systems including the Internet.
Knowledge of client and transactional monitoring processes.
Detail oriented with the ability to multitask and quickly adapt to changing assignments.
Ability to work autonomously and with teams in different locations.
Highly effective communication with all levels of the organization.
Ability to anticipate, draw conclusions, and adapt to changing needs and demands.
Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of staff and management.
Strong analytical skills, problem solving, strategic thinking and reasoning abilities.
A high degree of integrity, professionalism, and capacity to excel in a cohesive team environment.

Associate’s degree and/or Bachelor’s Degree.
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (CAMS), or other relevant professional certification.
Experience performing AML and financial crime investigations, customer due diligence reviews and/or sanctions screening reviews.
Experience working in AML software solutions including transaction monitoring systems, customer risk rating systems, and/or case management tools like Actimize, Verafin, Fiserv, FCRM, Jack Henry Yellow Hammer, Patriot Officer.
General banking compliance knowledge.
Experience working in a professional services or project-based environment.
Expertise in common financial crime technology platforms like CLEAR, LexisNexis, World Check etc.
Prior financial crime consulting experience.
Bilingual Spanish.

Excellent judgment, organization, attention to detail and commitment to confidentiality and high-quality client service.

Predictable delivery against engagement milestones and timely resolution of risks and escalations.
Improved visibility into capacity, chargeability, realization, margins and receivables.
Consistent adoption of standardized engagement processes, documentation and account reporting.
Effective handoffs from transaction close to recurring services and stronger cross-service-line collaboration.

title: Associate Manager, Logistics, DoorDash for Business
description:
About the Team
DoorDash for Business is building the premier corporate dining and benefits platform—helping companies of all sizes feed their teams through industry-leading products and meal programs. Our mission is to become the go-to solution for executives, administrators, and employees who need seamless, high-quality food programs at work. We move fast, operate with an ownership mindset, and are growing new product lines to better serve our corporate customers.
About the Role
As an Associate Manager on the DoorDash for Business Catering team, you will own the Dasher and delivery experience for catering—making sure large, high-stakes catering orders show up on time, get handed off and set up correctly, and reach the customer the way they expect.
You'll work at the intersection of operations, logistics, and analytics—getting deep into the details of how catering deliveries actually play out on the ground, forming hypotheses about what's breaking, and running small, fast tests to find what works before we scale it. This is early-stage, hands-on problem solving, not optimizing a machine that already runs.
You will report into the Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations for DoorDash for Business and can work remotely or hybrid depending preference.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own Dasher quality for catering: Take end-to-end ownership of delivery quality for catering—on-time arrival, accurate drop-off and setup, and a clean handoff—so customers can trust every order.
Build net new logistics: Figure out how catering and deliveries should actually work—Dasher selection, batching, timing, equipment, and handoff—by testing different approaches and learning what holds up in the real world.
Get into the details: Dig into individual deliveries, talk to Dashers and customers, and trace exactly where things break down—then turn those root causes into concrete operational fixes.
Use AI to optimize how we operate : Build the automated workflows that show where catering deliveries break down—and lean on AI to turn slow, manual analysis and one-off fixes into repeatable processes the team can scale.
Influence the Product Roadmap: Translate what you learn on the ground into clear product and operational recommendations that make catering delivery more reliable.
We're excited about you because…
You have 4–6 years of experience in strategy & operations, logistics, management consulting, or a high-growth marketplace environment.
You have a track record of owning cross-functional operational problems end-to-end—from diagnosis to testing to rollout—and are comfortable building from scratch in ambiguous, early-stage environments.
You have experience owning partner-team relationships and working closely with Product and Engineering.
You're analytically strong: you write SQL, work fluently with data, and know how to get to the root cause and turn complexity into clear recommendations.
You demonstrate fluency with AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar) to automate workflows, surface insights, and drive faster, better decisions.
You communicate with clarity and influence—you can tailor your message for Dashers, operators, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership alike.
You love getting into the weeds—you'll happily roll up your sleeves, get to the lowest level of detail, and run the test yourself to find out what works.

description:
About the Team
We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…

Operational Intelligence is a technical team within our Technical Operations organization, developing the internal applications, data integrations, and AI-powered workflows that help our robotics fleet operate reliably and efficiently. We work directly with fleet support, service, Engineering, and Product teams to turn operational challenges into practical technical solutions. As a Senior Associate, Operational Intelligence, you will build and maintain applications, integrations, and automation that improve how our teams operate. This is a hands-on individual contributor role within Technical Operations, with software development as a core responsibility. We are looking for someone who brings strong systems experience: understanding how frontend and backend services fit together, how APIs connect them, and how software is built, deployed, and operated in production.You will own defined features and projects from understanding the operational problem through development, testing, rollout, and ongoing support. title: Senior Software Engineer, Proactive Security - Platform
description:
About the Team
At DoorDash we're building the industry's most scalable and reliable delivery network to support our three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and Dashers. Security Engineering is paramount to the success of our business, and DoorDash Security aspires to be one of the world's most admired Security Engineering teams. We are committed to building the world's most trusted on-demand logistics engine for delivery! We're expanding our team of great minds to help us secure and maintain a 24x7, no downtime, global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash's multi-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and Dashers.
About the Role
Our Proactive Security Engineering team is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Proactive Security - Platform to build the paved paths that engineers across DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo use to access infrastructure, manage secrets and authenticate services.
You will be part of our inclusive, collaborative global Security Engineering Platform team responsible for building and operating tier-0 security services for access management, secret storage and identity, including our in-house Access Platform, Teleport and HashiCorp Vault. Your job is to make the secure path the easiest path: self-service, well documented, and built into the tooling engineers already use every day.
This is a US remote position reporting directly to the Manager of our Proactive Security Engineering Platform team.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design, build and operate paved paths for privileged access, secrets management and identity on top of our access management and secret storage platforms.
Build self-service tooling, SDKs, Terraform modules and integrations that let engineering teams adopt just-in-time access, short-lived credentials and dynamic secrets without filing a ticket.

title: UTM Engineer - DoorDash Air
description:
About the Team
The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale.
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.
About the Role
We're hiring a Senior UTM Engineer who will build core components of DoorDash Air's internal route planning and airspace deconfliction stack — the systems that decide where our aircraft can safely fly, coordinate that with other operators and airspace authorities, and keep our internal stakeholders and external systems talking to each other in terms they understand. This is a role for someone who has already lived through the full lifecycle of a distributed, interoperable, uptime-critical system in a field where getting it wrong has real consequences — aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or similar — and wants to bring that judgment to a fast-moving aerial delivery network.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design, build, and deploy interoperable services that must pass rigorous, often open-source, conformance and integration testing against external systems and partners.
Develop novel path planning and airspace deconfliction algorithms that find safe, efficient routes through real-world, dynamic environments.
Build tools that help our teams and systems evaluate and optimize airspace efficiency and utilization.
Design integrations that connect the deconfliction stack to existing DoorDash systems, translating mission and airspace status into terms internal stakeholders can act on.
Collaborate closely with systems engineering, commercial operations, and flight operations to ship features that hold up in real-world flight.
Represent DoorDash Air externally — engaging with peer companies, working groups, and standards bodies to improve interoperable deployments industry-wide and help shape the
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

description:

The Senior Manufacturing Engineer role is a senior-level, hands-on manufacturing engineering position responsible for defining how custom parts are built and priced—reviewing manufacturability, generating competitive quotes, and providing design feedback that brings products to market faster. The role serves as a technical authority who helps raise the bar for costing and DFM (Design for Manufacturability) quality across regions.
MISUMI Americas serves three sets of customers—builders who order parts through us, manufacturing partners who make and assemble those parts, and our world-class sales professionals who rely on fast, accurate quoting and DFM support to win and serve accounts. This role sits at the interface of all three. As a senior member of the team, this person also coaches and mentors other engineers and partners closely with the Global Capability Center (GCC) Costing and DFM team, with room to grow their scope and influence over time.
Manufacturing Engineering & Quoting
● Release package review — Analyze models, drawings, parts lists, and other data to determine scope of work, manufacturing feasibility, requirements, and minimum lead time.
● Quoting — Combine engineering analysis with platform recommendations to generate quotes for builders or collaborate with external suppliers to determine the parameters needed to quote.
● Cost calculator generation — Use fabrication expertise and an understanding of process cost drivers to build cost calculators that bring quoting in-house for new service offerings.
● DFx feedback — Provide design-for-manufacturability and design-for-assembly feedback to builders, recommending changes that improve manufacturability, reduce part cost, or ease assembly.
● Automation feedback — Feed insights back to the quoting software team to improve the accuracy of automated quoting across manufacturing services.
● Drawing generation — Produce high-quality 2D drawings per ANSI/ASME Y14.5 standards.
Mentorship & Cross-Functional Collaboration
● Coaching & mentorship — Coach and mentor engineers on the US and GCC Costing and DFM teams, sharing fabrication and costing expertise to help them grow.
● Best practices & peer review — Help establish and document costing and DFM best practices, review work, and provide feedback that improves technical accuracy and consistency across regions.
● Cross-functional leadership — Lead through influence across engineering, sourcing, sales, quality, and software, aligning stakeholders on costing and DFM decisions without relying on direct authority.
● Dotted-line coordination — Guide and coordinate the technical work of engineers who do not report to this role (including GCC and cross-regional partners) and keep shared initiatives on track.
All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
● 4-year Mechanical Engineering degree or equivalent technical training.
● 5–10 years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering, costing/DFM, or related custom mechanical hardware work.
● Hands-on experience across multiple custom mechanical manufacturing processes (sheet metal, urethane casting, injection molding, etc.); CNC machining and 3D printing experience is a must.
● Strong understanding of GD&T and conventional (coordinate) tolerancing, and deep knowledge of the manufacturability and limitations of common metals and plastics.
● Experience mentoring or coaching other engineers and acting as a technical resource; collaborating with offshore/GCC teams is a plus.
● Proven ability to lead through influence and coordinate cross-functional or dotted-line teams without direct reporting authority.
● Thrives with a high degree of autonomy—owns their workload end to end, exercises sound technical judgment independently, and drives decisions to closure in a remote environment with minimal oversight.
