title: Head of Marketing - Bolingbrook, IL
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
Formic's Marketing Team is the growth engine behind our commercial expansion. We move fast, experiment boldly, and build systems that scale. We work in close lockstep with Sales, RevOps, and Leadership to generate pipeline, sharpen our message, and get in front of the right manufacturers at the right time. This team is small, high-impact, and driven - and we're looking for someone who can match that energy.
About this role:
As our Head of Marketing, you will build, optimize, and lead a scalable engine for creating demand and qualified pipeline. You will own how Formic shows up in the market, how we identify and reach the manufacturers we can help, and how we turn that engagement into high quality opportunities for Sales.
This is a broad, hands-on role spanning Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering and managing a team to deliver across those areas. You'll bring those capabilities together around a common goal: creating qualified pipeline and quantifying through data and insights what's driving it. As Formic grows, you'll help determine how the team and these capabilities evolve.
We're looking for someone who combines creativity with operating rigor. You'll set strategy, but you'll stay close enough to the work to understand what's actually happening. You'll establish clear priorities, ownership, and metrics, and make decisions based on results. When something works, you'll scale it. When it doesn't, you'll change it or stop doing it.
You'll also build and develop the team around you. That means setting clear expectations, delegating real ownership, coaching people to get better, and holding the team accountable for results. We want a leader who welcomes challenge, seeks out evidence that their assumptions may be wrong, and changes course when the data or the team tells them something different.
This is a builder role. One day you might be sharpening Formic's positioning; the next, reviewing pipeline performance with Sales, coaching an SDR, digging into why a campaign isn't converting, or working with a GTM Engineer to test a completely different way of reaching manufacturers. You should be equally comfortable asking "What should we try?" and "Did it work?"
We're not looking for someone to bring us a standard B2B marketing playbook or generate activity for activity's sake. We want someone who creates focus from ambiguity, turns experiments into learning, turns learning into repeatable systems, and can clearly connect the work of their organization to business results.
You will own the engine that feeds our sales and deployments.
In this role you will:
Own Brand & Marketing
Own Formic's marketing strategy and how we show up in the market.
Develop and continually sharpen our positioning, messaging, and story.
Translate Formic's technology, business model, and customer value proposition into messaging that resonates with manufacturers and their economic buyers.
Own content, creative, video, website, customer stories, events, campaigns, thought leadership, PR, product marketing, and other channels that build awareness and demand.
Develop differentiated messaging across industries, use cases, personas, and stages of the buying journey.
Turn customer outcomes, deployments, product capabilities, and what we're learning in the field into compelling content.
Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.
Own Demand & Pipeline Generation
Own the creation of qualified pipeline across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.
Build Our GTM Innovation Capability
Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.
Own the Funnel and the Numbers
Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.
Create Focus and Accountability
Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.
Build and Lead the Team
Lead and align a multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.
Bonus points if you have:
Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, industrial technology, or similarly complex B2B markets with long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers.
Experience directly building or leading SDR organizations, including account-based and territory-based outbound strategies.
Experience building or leading GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, or similar technical growth capabilities.
What Success Looks Like

2+ years of hands-on field service or maintenance experience supporting robotic or industrial automation systems
Solid troubleshooting skills across electrical, mechanical, PLC, or robotic control systems

Experience using CMMS platforms to track and report maintenance activity
Comfortable with local travel up to 80% and overnight travel up to 50%
Clear written and verbal communicator capable of producing structured service documentation

As Director, Distribution & Transportation for our Security business, you'll own the strategy behind that promise: the multi-site distribution network, the carrier partnerships, and the long-term direction of how we move product.
This is a seat with real scope. You'll lead the team that runs the network, sit at the table with commercial and operations leaders, and own the service performance our customers feel every day.

RESPONSIBLIITIES:
Establish and execute the distribution, transportation, and network strategy for the Security business, aligning logistics capabilities with growth objectives, customer expectations, and operational requirements.
Lead a multi-site distribution network, ensuring safe, efficient, and cost-effective operations across all facilities.

Partner closely with Commercial, Operations, Manufacturing, Customer Service, Procurement, and Supply Chain leadership to drive cross-functional initiatives and business results.

Lead annual logistics and transportation planning processes, including budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Manage third-party logistics providers (3PLs), warehouse partners, and transportation vendors to ensure performance expectations and contractual obligations are met.
Evaluate emerging technologies, systems, and automation opportunities that enhance visibility, productivity, and customer experience across the distribution network.
Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing team, creating organizational capability, succession plans, and career development opportunities.
Ensure compliance with all applicable transportation, safety, regulatory, and environmental requirements.
Provide executive-level reporting and recommendations regarding network performance, strategic opportunities, risks, and investment priorities.
Set the distribution and logistics strategy for the Outdoors business and shape its long-term direction.
10+ years of leadership experience across transportation, logistics or supply chain.
A bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Finance, Business Administration, Marketing or a related field — or equivalent experience. MBA preferred.
Demonstrated success leading a multi-site distribution network.
Experience managing carrier relationships, including negotiations and performance management.
A track record of leading teams, influencing stakeholders and driving cross-functional initiatives.
Accountability for service metrics — on-time, in-full and damage-free delivery.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 30%.

title: Lead Inspector & Stacker
description:
YOUR ROLE
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Lead and support production team members to meet daily manufacturing targets.
Communicate shift goals, updates, and expectations clearly to team members.
Serve as a role model for attendance, performance, and workplace behavior.
Support shift handoffs by communicating key updates and issues to maintenance or supervisors.
Inspect boards and ensure visual and dimensional quality standards are met.
Use QA inspection tools to measure the quality of products.
Follow QA standards to ensure we are producing a quality product.
Provide proper training for all new end of line associates.
Monitor and provide coaching and feedback regarding work performance of end of line associates.
Communicate with extruder operators to ensure a quality end product.
Review work order and ensure correct tags and color.
Manage line documentation.
Ensure packaging specification are met.
Ensure clean and organized work areas are maintained in accordance with 6S and housekeeping standards.
Adheres to Fiberon’s safety requirements.
Assist with managing the production floor (breaks, absences, etc.)
WORK ENVIRONMENT
Manufacturing environment with exposure to: Heat, noise, dust, and moving machinery
May require availability outside of standard hours to support troubleshooting or continuous operations.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Strength & Endurance Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull objects weighing between 20 to 50 pounds independently (over 50 pounds with buddy lift), including cleaning equipment, dust collection systems, and raw materials.
Perform repetitive tasks such as sweeping, brushing, vacuuming, and operating tools like staple guns and banders.
Stand and walk for extended periods (8 to 12-hour shifts) during production and cleaning tasks.
Maintain stamina and focus to perform physically demanding tasks without fatigue.
Mobility & Flexibility Bend, squat, stoop, kneel, crawl, and stretch to reach and clean various areas, inspect equipment, and align materials.
Climb ladders and work at heights to access dust accumulation and perform maintenance tasks.
Reach or work above shoulder level as needed.
Dexterity & Coordination Use hand tools such as brushes, brooms, scrapers, and vacuums with precision and good hand-eye coordination.
Handle packaging materials, attach labels, and refill equipment accurately and efficiently.
Visual & Sensory Acuity Good vision required to identify dust accumulation, inspect product quality, and monitor screens and labels.
Ability to perform color and defect inspections with close attention to detail.
Maintain balance and spatial awareness to ensure safety and stability in a dynamic environment.
Environmental Tolerance Work in hot, noisy, dusty, and/or humid conditions for extended periods.
Tolerate exposure to moving mechanical parts, vibrations, and varying temperatures.
Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) such as masks, respirators, safety glasses, earplugs, and gloves for long durations.
Communication & Safety Communicate effectively with team members regarding defects, operational issues, and safety concerns.
Recognize personal physical limits and request assistance when tasks become too demanding.
QUALIFICATIONS
High school diploma or equivalent
Additional technical, manufacturing, or quality-related training preferred
EXPERIENCE
Minimum 1-3 years of manufacturing preferred
Previous experience in product inspection, stacking , packaging, or material handling preferred
Experience in composite decking, plastics, wood-plastic composites, or related manufacturing environments preferred
Prior leadership, training, or team lead experience preferred

description:

Primary Function of Position
The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Working alongside senior epidemiology, data science, and market access colleagues, the intern will contribute analyses that inform value propositions and may help translate findings into inputs for budget impact or other economic models. The internship culminates in a final presentation to Future Forward leadership and cross-functional partners.
Essential Job Duties
Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology.
Coding & Cohort Definition: Identify and validate CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG code sets to define target populations, procedures, comorbidities, and outcomes; document code lists and assumptions so they can be reused by the team.
Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines.
Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study.
Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation.
Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant.
Required Skills and Experience
Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes.
Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis.
Proficiency in SAS and/or R and working knowledge of SQL
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences.
Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period.
Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined.
University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements:
University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Required Education and Training
Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level.
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines.
Familiarity with Medicare payment methodologies (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/APC, MPFS/RVU) and how coding drives payment across sites of service.
Research experience in medical devices, surgery, or procedural care.
Peer-reviewed publications or congress abstracts (e.g., ISPOR, AcademyHealth).
Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).

description:

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Position Overview
The Reimbursement Operations & Field Market Access lead is the execution engine of the U.S. HEMA organization. This role is the closest link to the sales and marketing organization and serves as the primary tactical interface with providers, payers, and field teams.
This is both a payer-facing and provider-facing role. On the payer side, this person develops value dossiers, manages payer advisory boards, and supports key account engagement. On the provider side, this person generates billing guides, fields customer reimbursement questions, develops provider education materials, and supports all field logistics related to coding implementation.
In Phase 1, this role carries both midstream and downstream responsibilities—from code acquisition and payment policy implementation through to field collateral generation and customer support. This person generates code and billing manuals, is responsible for all field logistics requiring implementation of new or existing codes, and directly fields customer questions regarding reimbursement.
This role carries shared responsibility for midstream/payment policy activities with the Upstream Strategist until a dedicated Midstream hire is made (~18 months). At that point, this role transitions to full downstream focus with outsourced or in-sourced field pull-through teams supporting product launches.
Core Responsibilities
Provider-Facing
Billing Guide Development: Create, maintain, and distribute comprehensive billing and coding guides for all products. Ensure guides are CPC-reviewed, compliance-approved, and updated with each code cycle.
Customer Reimbursement Support: Serve as the primary point of contact for management of customer reimbursement vendor(s).  Manage vendor, monitor performance, and retain required documentation.
Code Implementation Logistics: Manage all field logistics associated with the implementation of new or existing CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes. Coordinate with provider sites to ensure smooth adoption of coding changes and cost capture.
Sales & Marketing Support: Generate evidence-driven, compliant field collateral in direct support of the sales and marketing organization.
Payer-Facing
Value Dossier Development: Coordinate with Upstream and distribute value dossiers and payer-facing evidence packages that communicate the clinical and economic value of the product portfolio.
Key Account Management: Manage fractional headcount resources and coordinate payer engagement at key accounts.
Policy Monitoring & Implementation: Track payer coverage policies, MAC LCDs, and commercial payer guidelines. Translate upstream payment policy developments into actionable field tools and communications.
Field Personnel Management for Payer Campaigns: Manage and direct field personnel in support of payer-focused campaigns. Coordinate field reimbursement specialists, outsourced resources, and account-level teams to execute payer engagement strategies, coverage initiatives, and pull-through programs at targeted accounts.
Shared Midstream / Payment Policy
Code Acquisition Support: Support CPT/HCPCS code acquisition activities in partnership with the Upstream Strategist, including preparation of supporting materials for AMA and CMS submissions.
Payment Policy Implementation: Translate CMS OPPS/PFS payment policy changes into operational guidance for the field. Develop communications for code changes, payment updates, and coverage determinations.
Reimbursement Calculator & Tools: Develop and maintain compliance-accurate reimbursement estimation tools for use by the sales team and provider accounts.
Qualifications
Required
4 year degree is required.
6+ years of progressive experience in medical device or pharmaceutical reimbursement , field market access, or payer relations
Direct experience developing billing guides, coding tip sheets, and provider reimbursement education materials
Strong working knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10 coding systems and hospital billing workflows (OPPS, ASC, physician office)
Experience managing payer relationships, developing value dossiers, and executing advisory boards
Demonstrated ability to work closely with sales and marketing teams in a commercial support capacity
Strong project management skills; ability to manage multiple simultaneous deliverables across products
Preferred
CPC (Certified Professional Coder) certification strongly preferred
Experience with field reimbursement team management (outsourced or in-house)
Familiarity with FCA/AKS compliance requirements for manufacturer-provided reimbursement guidance
Experience with business intelligence platforms

It is also an opportunity to join a fantastic team with a great culture that focuses on the how as much as on the what. We want a leader who can build a compelling vision for the function, leads with integrity and humility, and is passionate about developing and caring for the team.
The Sr. Director is accountable for the global indirect spend portfolio and for building a best-in-class procurement function. The role drives measurable value through strategic sourcing, category management and supplier partnerships, makes buying simple for stakeholders, strengthens compliance and risk management, and uses data and AI to raise the function's impact.
Essential Job Duties
The Sr. Director, Head of Global Enterprise Procurement leads the global indirect procurement function, partners closely with Finance, Legal, IT, Operations and Commercial leaders, and is a trusted advisor to the executive team on spend, suppliers and third-party risk. The Sr. Director will:
Vision, Strategy and Leadership
Develop and communicate a clear multi-year vision and roadmap for a best-in-class function, including operating model, capabilities, technology and talent.
Lead, mentor and develop the team across procurement operations, sourcing, contracts, and travel and events, with clear performance measurement, career paths and succession plans.

Supplier Relationship and Risk Management
Rationalize the supplier base and build long-term partnerships with strategic suppliers, supported by a supplier performance and business review program.
Partner with Legal, Information Security, Quality and Compliance to manage supplier risk (financial, cyber, concentration, geopolitical and disruption) and to ensure contracts address regulatory and legal requirements.

title: Sr Mgr Supplier Engineering
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
The Senior Manager Supplier Engineering will lead a team of engineers responsible for the manufacturing process selection, supplier selection & qualification of components for Intuitive's next-generation robotic platforms.
This leader will drive supplier engagement and technical strategy across a diverse set of technologies including motion control systems, electromechanical assemblies, electronics, and precision mechanical components. The role requires close partnership with multiple product development partners across Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Operations, Quality, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing Engineering, and Program Management functions to ensure successful execution of New Product Introduction (NPI) objectives.
The ideal candidate combines strong technical leadership with exceptional cross-functional influence and a demonstrated ability to build and lead high-performing teams in complex, fast-paced product development environments.
Essential Job Duties
Lead and develop a team of Supplier Engineers by providing technical direction, coaching, career development, and organizational leadership
Own supplier engineering strategy for critical technologies as it relates to NPI programs
Drive supplier selection, qualification, development, and technical risk mitigation activities
Partner with ancillary Engineering and Sourcing teams to influence architecture, supplier engagement strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions
Lead technical assessments of supplier capabilities, manufacturing readiness, quality systems, and scalability
Drive design-for-manufacturability and design-for-supply-chain excellence throughout product development
Partner with Program Management to identify, communicate, and mitigate program risks.
Provide leadership in supplier selection, technical assessment, cost optimization, performance improvement, and manufacturing readiness for these technologies: Motor assemblies
Encoders and sensing technologies
Gearboxes
Brakes and actuation mechanisms
Bearings, rails, ball screws, and precision motion hardware
Printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs)
Cable assemblies and interconnect systems
Precision machined components
Castings and forgings
Sheet metal assemblies
Build strong partnerships across ancillary engineering, operations, quality, sourcing, manufacturing, and executive leadership teams
Influence technical and business decisions without direct authority
Facilitate alignment among diverse stakeholders with competing priorities
Communicate effectively at both executive and working-team levels
Required Skills and Experience
Proven ability to lead teams to solve complex technical and process problems
Proven ability to hire highly capable staff, and grow and mentor staff
Proven ability in New Product Introduction
Outstanding analytical skills along with good judgment
Strong knowledge of GD&T required.
Proficient in Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing techniques
Proficient in pFMEA, process validation, route cause investigation, inspection, and test techniques
Knowledge of document management systems and ERP Systems, preferably Agile and SAP
Knowledge of 21 CFR part 820 and ISO 13485 preferred
Demonstrable knowledge of a wide range of manufacturing processes, including an understanding of key input variables for quality, cost, and capacity
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentations to executives
Demonstrated Project Management skills
Experience in a high-volume medical device company is a plus
Ability to travel to suppliers on an as-needed basis – domestic and international (25%)
Required Education and Experience
BSE degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or equivalent (advanced degree preferred)
10 or more years related experience in Manufacturing, Operations, Supplier Development, or related field with significant medical or medical device experience preferred
Minimum 3 years of experience leading component or supplier development, or leadership of equivalent areas

Primary Function of Position:
The mission of Supplier Engineering is to ensure high quality and stable delivery of purchased production components from suppliers operating under robust quality systems . Each supplier engineer is responsible for ensuring suppliers meet ISI requirements for product quality, cost, and service.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Part Qualification
Support Value Engineering and Quality Improvement Part Qualification efforts
Lead Core Product Teams in defining appropriate Part Qualification requirements This includes defining testing and inspection requirements prior to system integration to maximize ISI factory efficiency
Support transfer of parts between suppliers

Support Manufacturing Line Escalations from manufacturing teams

Manufacturing Process Selection and Development
Lead manufacturing process selection
Identify the correct process for manufacturing the part, considering process quality, long term capacity and total lifecycle cost.
Identify where DFM is appropriate to achieve higher quality, lower costs or better supply chain capacity
Educate internal customers and suppliers regarding supplier quality, process and operational capabilities, best value manufacturing methods and tooling for key supplier processes
Manage change
Drive improvements to ISI requirements as necessary by proposing and managing changes to specifications and drawings through the ECO process
Manage the planning and implementation of supplier change management projects using the Supplier Change Request process (SCR) post Design V&V
Provide status of the readiness (quality, capacity, delivery) of the supply chain for major production process changes
Work cross-functionally to improve supplier engineering processes
Supplier Selection and Evaluation
Support Supplier Selection
Work with Product Design, Commodity Mangers and other stake holders to identify high capability suppliers necessary for New Products based on assessment of business need and supplier capability.
Evaluate new supplies through informal assessments and formal assessment by supporting lead auditors in QMS evaluations
Foster Supplier Relationships
Support audit team in addressing findings to develop suppliers’ quality and business systems in order to meet ISI’s requirements
Manage supplier relationships to effectively partner with ISI suppliers

In order to adequately perform the responsibilities of this position the individual should possess:
BS degree in Engineering field
8+ years related experience in Manufacturing, Supplier Process Engineering, Design, or related field
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience creating and aggregating DFM feedback
Demonstrable knowledge in evaluating and challenging supplier technical, quality, and business capabilities
Experience with a wide range of manufacturing processes including understanding of key input variables for quality, cost and capacity Desired product experience in the following categories: Machining, including 4 & 5-axis holdings, FMS and bar-fed lathes
Plastic Injection Molding or other plastic forming processes
Die casting or Thixomolding
Proven ability to motivate suppliers and lead teams to solve difficult technical and process problems
Knowledge of pFMEA, process validation, inspection and test techniques
Familiarity with 21 CFR part 820 and ISO 13485 Experience in auditing suppliers to these standards is preferred
At a minimum, candidate should understand GDP and QMS methods
Significant computer experience using Windows, Word, Excel, Access and ERP Information Systems, preferably SAP
Ability to read and interpret detailed specifications and schematics and communicate technical information
Experience in a medical device company is a preferred
Experience with low-volume high-mix production environments is a preferred
Ability to travel to suppliers on an as needed basis – domestic and international

Competitive Insights and serve as a strategic partner to da Vinci product teams, global
marketing teams, and regional and local commercial stakeholders. This role delivers actionable
competitive insights and deeper analysis of priority competitors to support product strategy,
competitive response, procedure growth, and business decision-making.
The successful candidate will combine technical, clinical, and business acumen to collect and
synthesize intelligence, identify emerging opportunities and risks, evaluate tradeoffs, and

making processes.

Business Development, Global Marketing, Engineering, Financial Planning and
Analysis, and regional teams.

core teams, so findings and recommendations are sharp, actionable, and jointly
owned.
o Advise senior leaders and cross-functional partners by translating complex
competitive dynamics into clear implications, strategic options, and

o Keep the organization’s vision and values at the forefront of decision making
and action.

 Clinical and technical depth and demonstrated ability to assess competitor solutions

 Excellent problem-solving, organizational, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

 Resourceful self-starter with the ability to work independently under pressure and

Analysis, Strategy, Marketing, and regional teams.
 Demonstrated strategic thinking and ability to create and execute research plans and

 Demonstrated ability to independently frame ambiguous, high-complexity business

recommendations.
 Fluency in reading and speaking Chinese.
Required Education and Training
 Bachelor’s degree with minimum 12 years of related experience, OR
 Advanced degree with minimum 8 years of related experience, OR PhD with minimum 5 years of related experience
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in one or more of the following: competitive intelligence, product management, clinical development engineering.
 Experience in the medical device, surgical robotics, or broader healthcare industry, with clinical and technical knowledge of complex capital equipment and associated technologies.

description:

Primary Function of Position:
The individual will lead design, development, and testing of components and sub-systems for existing and next generation Endoluminal instruments, steerable catheter-based devices, and accessories that will interface with a robotic system. This role serves as a key technical contributor and leader, responsible for complex design challenges, project leadership, and advancing solutions through the product development process. The candidate will work within a technical team and with outside suppliers to develop and evaluate new technology solutions, establish design requirements to meet customer and company needs, prototype and refine designs, and advance them through the product development process to commercialization.
The successful candidate must excel in a fast-paced team environment and be capable of creative and efficient problem solving while ensuring attention to detail and quality when faced with time pressures. The individual must possess the technical expertise to understand complex mechanical designs and a passion for integrating quality into products. A strong sense of shared responsibility and commitment to high product quality is essential.
Essential Job Duties
Design, prototype, troubleshoot, and optimize components and subassemblies of rigid and flexible catheter structures
Evaluate component and subsystem designs within the context of overall system performance, reliability, manufacturability, and user experience.
Establish technical direction, driving trade-off decisions, and influencing cross functional teams
Collaborate cross functionally to understand and drive clarity on clinical, usability, and business needs, and decompose these needs into design requirements.
Drive rigorous understanding of design risks by learning not just how a design behaves, but why.
Complete detailed drawings and conduct tolerance analysis statistical best practices appropriately.
Drive failure investigations using rigorous but efficient experimental plans.
Prepare protocols/reports/summaries/readouts to capture and communicate design progress and defend / propose design decisions.
Develop and improve test methods and assembly fixturing to support building and testing on prototypes.
Collaborate cross functionally with supplier engineers, manufacturing process development engineers.
Review design changes on existing products for impact on regulatory and manufacturing
Mentor and guide technicians and junior engineers.
Required Education and Training
·         Bachelor's in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent
Required Skills and Experience
Minimum 6 years of experience in a mechanical design or catheter design role.
Proficiency using CAD to create, fabricate, and document medical device designs.
Experience with a range of prototyping and fabrication methods, including 3D printing, extrusion, injection molding, machining, wire EDM, welding, etc.
Proven ability to apply (or learn where needed, then apply) engineering first principles to understand and achieve quick and reliable solutions to engineering problems.
Exceptional mechanical aptitude and visual thinking skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, utilizing engineering tools such as finite element analysis, statistics, and experimental designs.
Proven ability to iterate prototypes and mock-ups rapidly.
Experience applying GD&T, tolerance stack analysis, and design-for-manufacturing principles.
Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills. Ability to present to a wide range of audiences.
Experience collaborating with multi-disciplinary internal functions like quality engineering, manufacturing engineering, clinical engineering, human factors, supplier engineering etc. and external suppliers
Strong understanding of all phases of Design Control
Proven ability to work well in a team environment as well as “solo” assignments.
Demonstrated ability to follow through / sense of urgency.
Self-starting, hands-on, and habitually curious.
Demonstrated ability to handle multiple complex priorities as a matter of routine.
Preferred Skills and Experience
MS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.
Experience with catheter design and manufacturing.
Understanding of mechatronics, robotics, and servo-controlled systems.
Experience developing requirements and performing risk assessment of candidate designs.
Demonstrated ability to be resilient, creative, and make progress when faced with organizational and project complexity and constraint.

title: Sr. PMC Technician
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The PMC Technician 3 works under general direction, follows applicable department procedures and follows oral and written instruction. This position requires a highly motivated team player to ensure Equipment, Fixture and Tooling are calibrated before their due date, according to current SOP, and to ensure any Equipment, Fixture or Tooling are available for manufacturing or inspection of any products manufactured on the site. This position executes Preventive Maintenance on time and according to applicable ERP systems and supports any Unplanned Maintenance in a timely manner. This position is responsible for reporting or escalating any equipment or fixture with low productivity to be evaluated or fixed, and any repair not covered by PMC documentation or work instructions.
Essential Job Duties
Follow all corporate, safety, and production procedures and regulations.
Maintain excellent attendance in accordance with Quality Operations guidelines.
Complete ISU and other required training courses on time.
Perform other duties as assigned, in compliance with performance targets set by department.
Record test logs or write daily activity reports as required
Escalate safety, quality or other issues with supervisor or manager as needed.
Perform routine inspections, lubrication, adjustments, and repairs on machinery to prevent breakdowns per work instructions and with appropriate tooling or fixtures as indicated by procedure.
Performs PM or Calibration before it expires (due date) including any top-level EFT and peripheral assets of such EFTs, and inputs results in the ERP/SAP system.
Record completed work on assets in ERP/ SAP and update the expiration date label on the asset for any EFT after PM or Calibration is performed.
Records on Quality Notifications that require an equipment event, describing problems and verification results.
Follow-up / fulfill equipment event (EEs) forms with cross-functional teams as needed.
Requests ECOs from the Engineering Department or QO Engineer to update or modify any PMC document that does not comply with current PMC activities
Issue asset numbers for new or modified tooling/fixtures and manage equipment retirement.
Coordinate with external service providers for off-site or on-site calibration and service.  Identifies new Vendors/Suppliers for equipment and spare parts.
Coordinate internal/external calibration, manage spare parts inventory, and issue and reconcile Purchase Orders (POs) for vendor services to ensure equipment uptime and adherence to ISO/FDA quality standards.
Create and manage a monthly/annual schedule for all preventative maintenance (PM) and calibration activities; works with external vendors to ensure prompt turnaround times on the external calibration of equipment.
Works closely with Engineering teams and vendors on acquiring newly developed EFTs and their delivery timelines
May require the physical packaging of assets to be transferred to outside vendors of other Intuitive sites.  May require filling out Shipping Authorization Forms (SAF) for the transfer of Assets/Inventories or equipment use.
Lead or participate in Continuous Improvement projects, kaizen or just do it events.
As required, provide support to production and/or Engineering during equipment and/or process validation.
Required Experience and Education
High School Diploma or Technical Career Degree
Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
5 years of working experience, preferably in manufacturing environment related to preventative maintenance
US sites: Ability to read, write, and understand English (MX preferred).
Proficient in the use of personal computers, including Microsoft Office suite
Conducting 6S maintenance.
Perform basic arithmetic (including decimals) and calculate averages, percentages, and ranges using a calculator as needed. Determine nominal, minimum, and maximum values from specifications and tolerances.
Follow standard instructions and apply practical judgment in routine, standardized situations with minimal variation
Ability to work effectively within their team, with cross-functional teams, and independently to achieve quality objectives.
Ability to perform extensive walking and repetitive physical motion (squatting, bending, lifting)
Strong time management skills
Attention to detail
A strong understanding of mechanical systems, including gears, bearings, motors, and shafts.
The ability to diagnose and resolve mechanical, electrical, and other technical issues quickly and effectively, pinpointing the root cause of malfunctions.
A strong understanding of mechanical systems, including gears, bearings, shafts, hydraulics, and pneumatics, for maintaining and repairing equipment.
Diagnose and repair electrical issues, including familiarity with wiring, control panels, and automation systems.
Knowledge of hydraulic and pneumatic systems, components and operation with the ability to quickly troubleshoot, identify and repair equipment malfunctions.
Understand and interpret technical documentation for understanding equipment and procedures.
Familiarity with PLCs and other software driven control systems used in manufacturing.
Understanding of Purchase Order process, invoice reconciliation and negotiation
Ability to perform master scheduling
Physical Requirements

The Staff Architect, Digital Applications is the technical and architectural leader responsible for defining and driving the long-term technology vision for the My Intuitive ecosystem.
This role is accountable for ensuring that all customer-facing digital capabilities evolve toward a single, integrated customer experience spanning mobile, web, and future AI-enabled experiences. The Principal Architect will partner closely with product, engineering, design, clinical, commercial, data, and platform leaders to transform My Intuitive from a collection of applications into a unified digital ecosystem and the digital operating system for robotic surgery.
The successful candidate combines deep software architecture expertise, customer-centric thinking, platform strategy, organizational influence, and the ability to align multiple product and engineering organizations around a common architectural north star.
Roles & Responsibilities
Ecosystem Vision and Architecture Leadership
Define and evolve the end-state architecture for the My Intuitive ecosystem.
Establish architectural principles, guardrails, reference architectures, and technical roadmaps aligned with business and customer objectives.
Drive convergence from fragmented applications toward a unified ecosystem anchored around common identity, customer journeys, data, and platform services.
Act as the chief architect for customer experience strategy across digital products and platforms.
Customer Experience Architecture
Champion a journey-centric architecture spanning Learn, Prepare, Perform, Review, Improve, and Mentor experiences.
Ensure experiences are designed around customer goals rather than organizational or application boundaries.
Define reusable experience patterns enabling consistent navigation, personalization, workflow orchestration, and engagement across the ecosystem.
Advocate for human-centered design principles and frictionless customer experiences.
Platform and Systems Architecture
Lead architecture across customer identity, entitlement, collaboration, learning, case management, insights, notifications, analytics, integration, and AI capabilities.
Drive platform-first approaches that maximize reuse, scalability, reliability, and maintainability.
Guide architecture for cloud-native platforms, APIs, event-driven systems, data products, AI services, and interoperability.
Ensure solutions support current and future Intuitive platforms and digital services.
Applications and AI
Establish architectural patterns enabling longitudinal customer journeys and personalized experiences.
Drive integration of AI-enabled workflows, recommendations, insights, learning pathways, and decision support capabilities.
Partner with Data Engineering, AI/ML, Clinical, and Product teams on future-facing digital experiences.
Cross-Functional Influence
Collaborate with leadership to translate long-term business strategy into technology investments and architectural roadmaps.
Align multiple engineering teams around common architecture standards and platform direction.
Mentor senior engineers, architects, and technical leaders across the organization.
Serve as a trusted advisor for strategic engineering decisions and major investments.
Governance and Technical Excellence
Lead architecture reviews and technical design governance.
Drive engineering quality, cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, safety, and regulatory considerations into architectural decisions.
Establish measurable architecture outcomes tied to customer experience, adoption, scalability, and business value.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.
12+ years of experience designing and delivering large-scale software platforms and digital products.
8+ years operating in senior architecture leadership roles.
Proven track record defining architecture strategies across multiple products, business domains, and engineering organizations.
Deep expertise in cloud-native architectures, distributed systems, APIs, microservices, event-driven architectures, and platform engineering.
Experience building customer-facing ecosystems serving multiple personas and workflows.
Strong understanding of identity, personalization, engagement, analytics, data platforms, and digital customer experiences.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior leadership and drive alignment across organizations without direct authority.
Exceptional communication and strategic thinking skills.

Experience building platform ecosystems that span mobile, web, cloud, edge, and connected device experiences.
Knowledge of AI-enabled customer experiences and intelligent workflow orchestration.
Experience defining multi-year technology strategies and organizational transformation initiatives.
Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field preferred.

Progress toward one My Intuitive ecosystem architecture.
Less duplication and technology fragmentation (reduce cost to serve).
Product Quality at expected levels.
Greater reuse of shared platform services.
More consistent customer experiences.
Higher adoption and engagement.
Faster delivery through reusable architecture.

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Vision Systems Engineer to join our multidisciplinary engineering team. This role offers the opportunity to work across a large portion of the product lifecycle—from development and design through verification, manufacturing, sustaining engineering, and field support.
As a hands-on technical team member, you will leverage expertise in electrical and optics to solve complex technical challenges, improve product performance, and drive continuous improvement. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to investigate field issues, enhance manufacturability and reliability, and contribute to the development of next-generation vision systems.
Success in this role requires technical depth, intellectual curiosity, strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, and a collaborative mindset. You thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy solving challenging problems, and are passionate about delivering robust, high-quality products that make a meaningful impact.
Key Responsibilities
Product Engineering & Technical Leadership
Lead technical investigations spanning design, manufacturing, and field performance throughout the product lifecycle
Conduct detailed root cause investigations for product, manufacturing, and field issues, developing effective corrective and preventive actions
Design, develop, test, validate, and implement engineering solutions to improve product performance, reliability, and manufacturability
Develop manufacturing processes to diagnose failures and repair returned products
Drive engineering decisions using sound technical judgment, data analysis, and structured problem-solving methodologies
Participate in and lead design reviews, technical discussions, and risk assessments to ensure design robustness and product quality
Mentor junior engineers by sharing technical knowledge, engineering best practices, and structured problem-solving approaches

Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and system-level issues using structured, data-driven root cause methodologies
Perform circuit analysis and electrical troubleshooting as required
Apply failure analysis techniques and collaborate with external analytical laboratories utilizing methods such as FTIR, X-ray imaging, SEM/TEM, EDS, and related technologies
Working knowledge of scripting or programming in Python, C, C++, C#, or JavaScript is desirable to support automation, analysis, and engineering workflows
Manufacturing & Supplier Development
Drive Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA), and Design for Serviceability (DFS) initiatives for components and subsystems
Partner with suppliers to improve component quality, manufacturability, and overall product performance
Support supplier qualification, manufacturing transfer, production ramp-up, and yield improvement initiatives
Collaborate with Manufacturing and Quality Engineering to support sustaining engineering and continuous product improvements

Demonstrated experience across multiple stages of the product lifecycle, including concept development, design, prototyping, verification, validation, manufacturing transfer, and sustaining engineering
Skilled at planning and executing experiments using modern test and measurement equipment
A hands-on engineer who enjoys solving challenging technical problems
Curious, analytical, and driven to understand root causes rather than symptoms
Passionate about designing reliable, manufacturable, and high-quality products
Comfortable working in fast-paced, highly collaborative environments
An effective communicator with strong presentation skills and confidence leading technical design reviews
Willing to travel up to 10% as needed to support suppliers, manufacturing, or development activities

title: Staff Mechanical Design Engineer
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
At Intuitive, we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. By combining ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints. We are looking for team members with exceptional character who have the capacity to simplify complex problems and the energy to deliver solutions urgently to our patients. Intuitive Accessories are the interface between all aspects of the da Vinci system and enable safe and effective robot-assisted surgery. Our customers interact directly with Accessories in every surgical procedure, and they serve a critical role in customer satisfaction and patient outcomes. The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer for Single-Port (SP) Accessories will support development and production of existing and new products. This position requires a hands-on, technically strong engineer to dive deep into solving engineering challenges, and to provide high-level assessment of risks and opportunities. Projects will include a mix of sustaining existing products and new product development, including improvements for cost savings and manufacturability to enable significant volume growth, enhancements to increase customer satisfaction, and improving reliability.
Essential Job Duties
• Drive Design efforts to optimize performance, manufacturability and reliability of existing and future Da Vinci SP Accessories.
• Develop components and product mechanical drawings in a regulated environment for high volume manufacturing processes, including plastic injection molding, thermoset compression molding, extrusion, and machining.
• Design for manufacturing and automation, sterilization processes, and biocompatibility.
• Work cross-functionally with Manufacturing Engineers, Systems Analysts, Clinical Development Engineers, Human Factors Engineers, and Supplier Engineers.
• Review and understand product functional requirements and design specifications.
• Provide mechanical engineering sustaining support for resolution of manufacturing and field issues.
• Investigate and determine root cause of design, manufacturing, or material issues.
• Research, understand, and design to relevant product-specific international standards.
• Develop, implement, test, and document solutions that meet clinical, functional, and product requirements.
• Perform and document risk analyses (FMEA) and implement effective mitigations, following design control processes.
• Help identify and develop vendors to manufacture components.
• Develop initial fixtures and processes to assemble components.
• Develop product and component verification testing and product validation testing
• Support production of final product by troubleshooting process and component problems
• Provide engineering support to Manufacturing, Materials, Test Engineering, and Service to facilitate transfer of designs.
• Develop, implement, test and document solutions for these opportunities according to corporate standard and departmental operating procedures
• Mentor other engineers and champion best practices for mechanical design
Required Skills and Experience
• Proficiency using CAD to design and document mechanisms; SolidWorks strongly preferred
• Good communication and documentation skills
• Experience in designing high volume consumable medical products
• Strong working knowledge of GD&T
• Experience with complex interface compatibility and tolerance analysis
• Demonstrated knowledge of high-volume component manufacturing processes (including injection molding, plastics films, extrusions, thermoforming, and plastic bonding methods)
• Demonstrated knowledge of materials (preferably plastics, silicones, polyurethanes, isoprenes) and material properties. Ability to apply knowledge of engineering materials and component selection criteria to product designs through strong concept development, design analysis, hands-on prototyping, and reliability testing skills.
• Demonstrated ability to think at a systems level, interface between multiple design groups, and negotiate conflicting requirements.
• Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer.
• A passion for solving tough technical problems - Strong mechanical intuition and persistence to drill down to pinpoint root cause of problems, solving problems using fundamental principles.
• Ability to communicate effectively (written, oral) across functions, including presenting to a technical audience
• Prior experience working in medical device or other regulated industry
Required Education and Training
• Minimum education: BS in Mechanical Engineering required, MSME preferred. Biomedical or other engineering discipline may be acceptable with appropriate mechanical experience.
• Minimum 12 years of hardware product design experience preferred with undergraduate degree; minimum 8 years with graduate degree
Working Conditions
• Ability to lift 30 lbs. without assistance.
Preferred Skills and Experience (As applicable - Specific skills, knowledge, and experience that
are not required to perform the job, but are desirable to have)
• Comfortable operating machine shop tools/equipment, Rapid prototype equipment (3-d printers, laser cutters etc.), measurement and test equipment
• Knowledge in additional manufacturing processes such as extrusion, blow molding, ultrasonic welding, RF welding, heat staking, and laser welding
• Comfortable with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis
• Ability to handle ambiguity effectively and oversee multiple projects at once
• Knowledge of ISO requirements and GMP guidelines. Experience with FDA regulations and medical device design control a strong plus
• Experience leading departmental or cross-functional projects/initiatives from concept through completion
• Knowledge of sterilization methods, biocompatibility, and packaging of medical devices

Primary Function of Position
We are looking for a hands-on leader to invest in and to grow our material handling team to the next level. This includes coaching, encouraging and empowering the team as well as working side-by-side with them in a cold chain environment. Key team tasks and metrics include receiving, put away, picking, material supply and inventory accuracy. This position is responsible for oversight of personnel, administration of the raw material and sub-assembly warehouse operations, 5S + safety, inventory accuracy, and internal material replenishment processes. There is a strong focus on continuous improvement in the role.
Essential Job Duties
Hire, train, develop, and motivate warehouse personnel to follow procedures, meet high level quality standards, production schedules, operations dept goals, and productivity requirements.
Make sure current processes are properly documented and drive process improvement and simplification.
Ensure freezers, dry goods warehouse, and work area are maintained to 5S standards and FIFO is adhered to with all material movements.
Continuously perform gap analysis on documents related to warehouse operations such as SOP, DOP, WI, VA, and update as required
Work with Inventory Control to analyze and correct issues related to storage quantities and inventory discrepancies.
Provide vision and direction to team and drive training to Lean Material flow practices.
Ensure that optimal inventory levels of commodities are maintained to meet production requirements.
Ensure that company procedures, including APHIS requirements, are understood and adhered to.
Responsible for managing employee training record completion and status.
Evaluate and provide annual performance feedback to direct reports along with interim counseling to ensure performance criteria are being met.
Implement Short-Term Problem Containment and Long-Term Corrective Action for warehouse issues.
Drive continuous improvement of current systems and processes and work closely with production planning and management to optimize the value stream opportunities.

description:
Job Description
The Maintenance Manager leads the Davenport plant maintenance, reliability, utilities and plant engineering agenda to support safe, compliant, reliable and cost-effective operations. What You Will Do
Lead maintenance work in accordance with company EHS requirements, safe work practices and applicable regulatory standards, including LOTO, electrical safety, machine safety, hot work, confined space, work at height and contractor safety.
Provide leadership and governance for ammonia refrigeration and Process Safety Management activities, including mechanical integrity, Management of Change, PHA and audit action closure, procedures, training and emergency preparedness.
Ensure maintenance activities protect food safety and product quality through hygienic maintenance, foreign-material prevention, approved lubricants, sanitary design, post-maintenance release and coordination with Food Safety & Quality and Sanitation.
Own deployment and maturity of the KHMS Maintenance, Reliability & Engineering pillar, including daily performance routines, monthly pillar reviews, 90-day plans and escalation of barriers.
Maintain asset hierarchy, functional locations, asset master data and criticality rankings in the CMMS, and develop maintenance strategies based on asset criticality.
Create and govern a rolling 52-week maintenance plan and a two-week detailed schedule aligned with production windows, labor, skills, parts, tools, permits and contractor resources.
Improve preventive and proactive maintenance effectiveness and reduce reactive work using failure analysis, Pareto reviews, root-cause problem solving, troubleshooting guides and condition monitoring where justified.
Partner with Production and Sanitation on planned downtime, handoffs, start-up readiness and rapid response while maintaining long-term reliability discipline.
Support reliable operation and maintenance of utilities and facilities, including ammonia refrigeration, HVAC, compressed air, electrical distribution, water and wastewater, as assigned.
Manage maintenance projects through prioritization, design review, procurement, installation, commissioning, documentation, training and handoff to operations.
Support OT infrastructure and security controls in partnership with site and enterprise OT/IT resources.
Build and manage the annual maintenance budget and monthly forecast, review spending with Finance and take corrective action on variances.
Lead spare-parts and storeroom governance, including critical spares, min/max levels, obsolescence, cycle counts, kitting, repairable spares and stock-out reduction.
Select and manage contractors and OEMs, including scope, safety expectations, deliverables, cost controls, documentation and performance reviews.
Lead, coach and develop maintenance leaders, planners, technicians, utilities personnel and apprentices while building skills, accountability, succession and engagement in a unionized manufacturing environment.
What You Bring
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Maintenance, Reliability, Operations or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience.
Progressive leadership experience in maintenance or reliability within a high-speed manufacturing environment. Food or beverage manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.
Experience leading maintenance planning and scheduling, preventive or predictive maintenance, CMMS/SAP work management, root-cause analysis, equipment reliability and maintenance cost control.
Working knowledge of industrial mechanical, electrical, controls/automation, utilities and facility systems.
Experience leading people, contractors, budgets and cross-functional improvement work in a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
Ability to analyze operational and financial data, translate losses into action plans, communicate across organizational levels and sustain execution routines.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with ammonia refrigeration and OSHA Process Safety Management or EPA Risk Management Program requirements.
Experience with KHMS, TPM, WCM or another integrated manufacturing excellence system.
CMRP, CRL, PMP, Lean/Six Sigma, refrigeration/PSM or a related technical certification.
Experience in a unionized facility and with food-safety systems such as FSSC 22000, HACCP and GMPs.
Experience with condition monitoring, asset criticality, reliability-centered maintenance, storeroom optimization or capital project delivery.

Work is performed in an office and active food-manufacturing environment with machinery, wet areas, temperature variation, noise and required personal protective equipment.
The role requires frequent presence on the plant floor, including stairs, platforms, production, maintenance, utility and warehouse areas.
The role must be able to support plant needs outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings, nights, weekends, shutdowns and emergency responses.

description:
Job Description
Job Purpose
As an Imaging Lab Scientist , you will support the development and execution of digital and physical visualization solutions that enable faster, clearer, and more confident packaging and product decisions across the Kraft Heinz North America portfolio. This role is responsible for delivering high-quality mock-ups, 3D models, 3D-printed parts, printed packaging materials, photography, and product documentation, while partnering with cross-functional teams to provide reliable, timely, and commercially relevant Imaging Lab support. The role also contributes creative problem-solving, concept translation, and innovative visualization approaches that help teams move from early ideas to actionable packaging decisions.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​ ​Support execution of Imaging Lab requests by delivering digital and physical mock-ups, 3D models, and 3D-printed outputs that help teams evaluate packaging and product concepts, communicate design intent, and accelerate decision-making
​Create and produce package and label print outputs across film, carton, adhesive, and related materials to support development, visualization, and business needs
​Develop and maintain quality guides, including color and defect guides, to support consistent evaluation standards and clear visual references
​Lead photography and product documentation activities to ensure accurate, high-quality visual records for projects and internal reference needs
​Operate the Kongsberg cutting table to produce precise physical mock-ups and support efficient execution of Imaging Lab deliverables
​Serve as a trainer for Kongsberg cutting table use, helping build capability and consistency across users as needed
​Support 3D modeling and 3D printing activities to create prototypes, concept models, and visualization tools that improve project understanding and development speed
​Manage multiple requests and projects concurrently across mock-ups, printing, guides, photography, and documentation while meeting agreed timelines and quality expectations
​Partner directly with cross-functional stakeholders including R&D, Marketing, Sales, Packaging Development, and external vendors to clarify needs, translate concepts into actionable visualization solutions, and deliver fit-for-purpose outputs
​Support early-stage concept development by helping teams convert ideas into practical visual, digital, or physical outputs that improve project understanding and decision-making
​
​Contribute innovative thinking and creative problem-solving to improve mock-up approaches, workflow execution, and the overall effectiveness of Imaging Lab support
​Support improvements in request intake, workflow coordination, and execution reliability to strengthen service levels and reduce errors or rework
​Maintain organized files, production records, and documentation to support continuity, traceability, and efficient handoffs
​Support safe, organized, and effective Imaging Lab operations through proper equipment use, adherence to lab procedures, and coordination of day-to-day execution needs​​
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in  Packaging, Graphic Communications, Design, or a related technical discipline, with 2+ years of relevant experience; advanced degree is preferred.
​Experience supporting digital and physical mock-up development, 3D modeling, 3D printing, package and label printing, photography, and product documentation in a lab, studio, or technical service environment
​Working knowledge of print production processes across film, carton, adhesive, and related packaging materials
​Experience developing or supporting visual quality standards such as color guides, defect guides, or comparable reference materials
​Demonstrated ability to operate technical production equipment, including cutting and mock-up systems such as the Kongsberg cutting table
​Experience with 3D modeling and prototyping tools, and the ability to create practical models or printed outputs that support packaging visualization and concept development
​Ability to train others on equipment use and support consistent execution of lab workflows
​Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple requests, timelines, and priorities with accuracy and responsiveness
​Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work closely with cross-functional partners and external suppliers to clarify needs and translate ideas into effective visualization solutions
​Demonstrated ability to document work clearly, maintain consistency in execution, and deliver outputs with quality and timeliness
​Experience translating early-stage concepts into practical digital or physical visualization outputs that support project development and decision-making
​ Demonstrated creativity and innovation in solving visualization, mock-up, prototyping, or packaging-related challenges, with the ability to suggest new approaches that improve execution or project outcomes
​ Knowledge of packaging materials, visualization methods, mock-up production workflows, 3D printing processes, and emerging digital tools or AI-enabled creative workflows is a plus
​Willingness and ability to support hands-on lab and production activities as required ​
