Job Description:
Key Responsibilities
Commodity Risk Management, Valuation & Reporting
Execute daily commodity risk management processes, including trade validation, trade reconciliation, exposure monitoring, and risk reporting across multiple commodities and regions.
Generate and maintain commodity exposure, hedge coverage, net open position, and market risk reports for business and leadership stakeholders.
Maintain and validate commodity forecast, pricing, position, and market data to ensure integrity and consistency across systems and reports.
Partner with Commodity Price Risk Managers to evaluate hedge structures, coverage strategies, and potential financial impacts of commodity market movements.
Support liquidity forecasting and reporting related to commodity hedging activities, including cash settlement requirements, margin obligations, and derivative-related cash flows.
Financial Analysis, P&L Attribution & Business Insights
Develop and maintain financial models, dashboards, and reporting tools to quantify commodity exposures, hedging performance, market risks, and business impacts across the global Mars Snacking portfolio.
Deliver P&L attribution and cause-of-change analysis, identifying key drivers of financial performance including commodity price movements, basis changes, hedge impacts, timing effects, and market structure shifts.
Conduct scenario analysis, sensitivity modeling, and risk and opportunity assessments to evaluate financial impacts and support strategic decision-making.
Support budgeting, forecasting, and business performance reviews by translating commodity market dynamics and hedging activities into clear financial outcomes.
Prepare executive-ready reporting and insights that communicate commodity exposures, financial impacts, risks, opportunities, and mitigation strategies.
Hedge Accounting, Financial Controls & Governance
Support hedge accounting programs through documentation, monitoring, and testing of designated hedging relationships in partnership with Treasury and Technical Accounting teams.
Perform prospective and retrospective hedge effectiveness testing to ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and maximize hedge accounting effectiveness.
Maintain a strong control environment around commodity transactions, trade validation, market data governance, curve management, and financial reporting processes.
Support internal and external audits by providing valuation support, reconciliation documentation, control evidence, and commodity risk reporting.
Ensure compliance with commodity risk management policies, financial controls, and governance requirements.
Systems, Data Management & Process Improvement

Reconcile data across CTRM platforms, broker statements, ERP systems, market data providers, and financial reporting systems.
Develop and enhance reporting and analytical solutions using Excel, VBA, SQL, Python, Power BI, Tableau, and other technology platforms.
Identify automation opportunities and drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, reporting accuracy, transparency, and controls.
Support implementation, testing, and ongoing enhancement of commodity risk management systems and technology platforms.
Planning & Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner closely with Treasury, Technical Accounting, Finance, Procurement, S&OP, Commercial Finance, and Commodity Price Risk Managers to support commodity risk management objectives.
Support demand forecast validation and volume planning processes that underpin commodity exposure and hedge management activities.
Support budgeting, forecast updates, cause-of-change reporting, and business performance reviews in collaboration with Finance Business Partners.
Provide analytical support for business planning, sourcing decisions, commodity strategy development, and financial performance management.
Build strong relationships across Treasury, Procurement, Planning, Manufacturing, Commercial, and Finance teams, providing insights and executive-ready reporting to support business decisions.

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Financial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related analytical field.
Strong understanding of global commodity markets, trading, hedging, valuation methodologies, and risk management principles.
Experience supporting commodity risk management, treasury, commodity trading, market risk, financial planning, product control, or commodity finance organizations.
Experience developing financial models that combine commodity pricing, sourcing assumptions, exposure forecasts, hedge results, and business drivers to assess P&L impacts.
Experience with commodity exposure reporting, Mark-to-Market valuation, trade reconciliation, hedge effectiveness testing, financial controls, and P&L attribution analysis.
Advanced analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to interpret complex datasets and deliver actionable insights.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with SQL, Python, VBA, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytical and reporting tools.
Experience with CTRM systems, ERP platforms, financial reporting systems, and market data providers preferred.
Demonstrated ability to perform data validation, reconciliation, valuation, financial analysis, and reporting in a fast-paced environment.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Excellent critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
Proactive mindset with a willingness to challenge discrepancies, improve processes, and recommend solutions.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to work effectively across global, cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated success operating within complex matrix organizations and collaborating with diverse internal and external stakeholders.

Knowledge of futures, options, swaps, OTC instruments, and hedge accounting methodologies.
Experience with independent price verification (IPV), P&L attribution, hedge effectiveness testing, and financial controls.

description:
Job Description:

As a PLC Technician, you will help transform our Bakery, one of the fastest growing and most loved brands in our category.  The transformation is enabled through significant investments in our existing “classic” production lines, as well as recently installed state-of-the-art production and packaging equipment.
Our staged transition toward a world-class maintenance program to support our operations will provide you with the opportunity to help install and maintain our physical assets, and then adopt and implement reliability programs to sustain their operational excellence.  All maintenance roles offer high-visibility and high-impact opportunities.  Proven maintenance leaders, experienced outside contractors, and a high-performing, tenured team of technicians will support your success onsite.
The day in the life of a Controls & Automation Technician:
Provides input to managing the controls and automation systems testing, quality control, data retrieval and training for packaging and processing equipment.
Assists in managing the controls and automation interface, testing, quality control, data retrieval, and training for all packaging and processing equipment.
Assists with the development and modification of PLC & HMI programs.
Provides project engineering support to process areas.
Provides controls support for the manufacturing facility and assist plant mechanics in troubleshooting.
Ensures documentation for control/electrical system and document change control procedures.
Assists with the development and management of controls related capital projects.
Contributes to determination and maintainability of new process control systems and manage process controls change control procedures for existing equipment.
You’ll work around moving machines – mixers, conveyor belts, and forklifts.
Knowledge, skills and Education:
All candidates, however, should have understanding in automated industrial machinery, which includes motors, servos, pumps, drives, relays, etc. and hydraulic and pneumatic systems; packaging, conveyance, liquid and powder manufacturing equipment and processes; PLC trouble shooting; electrical and mechanical drawings; installation and troubleshoot basic three phase motor control circuits; and breakdown analysis as well as the following:
Ability and skills to troubleshoot and maintain Allen-Bradley MicroLogix and ControlLogix hardware
Perform Allen-Bradley PLC programming implementing RSLogix5, RSLogix500 and RSLogix5000 software or equivalent.
Implement and troubleshoot industrial communication networks including Ethernet, Allen-Bradley Remote I/O and DeviceNet communication networks
Read electrical schematics, Process & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID’s) and Process Flow Diagrams (PFD’s)
Perform PID Loop tuning and implement instrument calibration procedures.
Knowledge of programming languages relevant to PLCs.
Install, maintain, and troubleshoot electrical control systems, including PLC controls, networking, and HMI systems.
Initiate and develop control system modifications and new projects to improve plant performance and reliability.
General knowledge of the National Electrical Code
Knowledge of Wiring, Hydraulic Systems, and Pneumatic Systems.
Reading blueprints and schematics.

Safety is a top priority for us. We provide protective gear and training to ensure a safe work environment.
Some activities may require standing in one place for long periods, lifting up to 40 lbs, walking around, or climbing stairs.

Job Description:
R&D Associate Scientist – Analytical Sciences
As an R&D Associate Scientist – Analytical Sciences, you will generate the analytical insights that support product innovation, quality growth, operational excellence, and sustainability across the Mars Snacking portfolio. Working in a collaborative laboratory environment, you will conduct testing on ingredients, materials, processes, and finished products while partnering with cross-functional teams to solve technical challenges and support business priorities.
This role is ideal for a scientist who is curious, adaptable, and eager to apply analytical and material science expertise to real-world product and ingredient development.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Food Science, Material Science or related science with 2+ years working experience in a laboratory
Proactive work behavior, forward thinking and able to make complex decisions that creates and delivers business solutions.
Experience performing analytical method protocols while working in compliance to quality standards and HSE protocols
Excellent attention to detail, analytical skills, and ability to work in compliance to Good Laboratory Practices and standards
Project management and good working knowledge of experimental designs
Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree in Chemistry, Food Science, Material Science or related science
3+ years of professional experience in the Analytical or Material Sciences field within the food, beverage, and/or confections industry
Knowledge and experience in advanced techniques, e.g. material and physical characterization (rheology, particle characterization, XRD, DSC) or imaging (digital/optical microscopy, XRT, SEM)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, problem solving, organizational and time management skills, and customer focus
Experience with executing operational responsibilities of a laboratory, including purchasing materials, equipment set up/operation/calibration, troubleshooting, training and preventive maintenance protocols, and proper chemicals management
Familiarity with statistical methods and basic ISO laboratory requirements

Performs all assigned analyses with minimal supervision upon training completion. Provides accurate and timely data and interpretation of results. Perform basic technical writing for the generation of routine standard operating procedures, test methods and other laboratory or quality protocols with guidance.
Supports or lead projects with guidance spanning troubleshooting, method development, continuous improvement projects, alignment scope intake in area of expertise, and data science related projects
Supports capability development including exploring and developing new technologies, method development, and training others in areas of proficiency and expertise
Adheres to Quality Management Systems (QMS), HSE and Good Lab Practices compliance and supports audits
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.

Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity.  The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands.  To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.  Access the tools, training and experience you need to have a positive impact on our business, on the planet, and most importantly on your own career.  Being a Mars associate is more than a job.  It’s the opportunity to start your tomorrow today.

This role is responsible for performing all reception and unloading operations for raw materials coming into the manufacturing facility. This position will also handle master sanitation activities for the area and perform required inventory tasks.

Perform receiving and unloading of all raw materials (bulks, liquids, super sacks, bags).

Manage and sign delivery documentation, noting any quality or quantity discrepancies.

Preferred: Knowledge of inventory control principles and ability to operate a forklift or scissor lift.
Physical/Environmental Requirements:
Ability to stand on a concrete floor for extended periods.
Must wear proper personal protective equipment (PPE).
Capable of bending, stooping, twisting, turning, reaching, and climbing stairs.
Ability to lift up to 55 lbs.

Inventory Management: Experience with tracking, counting, and managing stock levels is directly applicable to maintaining the WMS and performing inventory cycles.

3+ years of manufacturing experience operating a variety of machines
2 years of work experience within manufacturing, or a technical and/or trade discipline
Demonstrated competency in computer and pc software including MS Office and email

title: Regional Distributor Manager, U.S.
description:
Job Description:
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food maker with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. Founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry across three major geographic regions.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here's the Scoop – Summary
The Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. is accountable for delivering sales growth, market share expansion, distribution gains, and execution excellence through Champion's distributor partners within an assigned region.
Reporting to the Director, U.S. Sales, Neighborhood Pet, this role serves as the primary business lead for distributor performance and development.
The Regional Distributor Manager translates national sales strategy into regional execution plans, ensuring distributors and their sales organizations are aligned to Champion's priorities and growth objectives.
This position drives business results through distributor leadership, joint business planning, retailer engagement, sales capability development, and disciplined performance management.
Success in this role is achieved by building strong distributor partnerships, improving execution at retail, developing distributor sales teams, and delivering profitable growth throughout the region.
This is a fully remote position, which will ideally sit near Boulder (CO), Dallas (TX), Phoenix (AZ) or Southern California (CA). Expect 40-50% of travel within assigned geography.
Responsibilities:
Distributor Performance Ownership
Own sales, distribution, and execution result across assigned distributor partners and territories.
Hold distributors accountable to annual sales targets, distribution objectives, promotional programs, and strategic growth priorities.
Monitor distributor performance through established KPIs and implement corrective action plans when required.
Regularly evaluate distributor effectiveness, market coverage, resource allocation, and return on investment.
Distributor Strategy & Business Planning
Develop and execute Joint Business Plans with distributor partners aligned to national sales objectives and growth strategies.
Identify opportunities to increase market penetration, distribution points, retailer productivity, and share growth.
Lead annual planning, forecasting, and business review processes with assigned distributors.
Align distributor investments and resources to maximize commercial performance and customer impact.
Driving Execution Through Distributor Sales Teams
Influence, coach, and develop Distributor Sales Representatives (DSRs) to improve execution and sales effectiveness.
Conduct regular market visits to evaluate retail execution, merchandising standards, assortment compliance, and promotional effectiveness.
Deliver sales training, product education, and business development support to distributor sales organizations.
Ensure execution excellence against merchandising, pricing, promotional, and distribution objectives.
Retail Customer Development
Partner with key regional and independent retail customers to support growth, distribution expansion, and customer satisfaction.
Conduct customer business reviews and identify opportunities to strengthen Champion's market position.
Support distributor teams in developing retailer-specific growth strategies and action plans.
Build trusted relationships that position Champion as a strategic partner.
Forecasting, Analytics & Financial Management
Maintain accurate regional forecasts and provide timely updates on risks and opportunities.
Manage trade investments and promotional spending to maximize ROI and profitability.
Analyze sales performance, market trends, customer results, and distributor productivity to identify opportunities for growth.
Provide regular business updates and recommendations to the Director, U.S. Sales.
Market Leadership
Represent Champion Petfoods at industry events, trade shows, distributor meetings, and customer engagements.
Deliver insights regarding competitive activity, consumer trends, market dynamics, and emerging opportunities.
Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to ensure successful execution of business initiatives.
Key Accountabilities
The Regional Distributor Manager will be measured on:
Regional sales and profitability growth
Distributor performance against annual operating plan
Distribution gains and market penetration
Retail execution and merchandising compliance
Forecast accuracy
Trade investment ROI
Distributor sales force capability development
Regional customer growth and retention
Achievement of strategic business plan objectives
What are we looking for?
Bachelor's degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive sales experience within the pet industry, consumer packaged goods, or a related distribution-driven environment.
Demonstrated success managing distributor relationships and driving growth through indirect sales channels.
Proven ability to develop and execute business plans that deliver revenue growth, distribution gains, and improved customer performance.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including forecasting, budgeting, business analysis, and ROI management.
Experience influencing and developing sales teams without direct reporting authority.
Excellent relationship-building, negotiation, and communication skills.
Ability to analyze market data and translate insights into actionable growth strategies.
Highly collaborative, self-motivated leader who thrives in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and sales reporting tools.
Ability to travel approximately 40-50% within assigned geography.
Why You'll Succeed
You take ownership of results and hold yourself and partners accountable.
You know how to win through distributors and indirect sales channels.
You build strong partnerships while maintaining high performance expectations.
You balance relationship management with data-driven decision making.
You are passionate about developing people, growing customers, and delivering exceptional execution in the market.
Mars Leadership Competencies
Drives Results
Plans & Aligns
Balances Stakeholders
Financial Acumen
Interpersonal Savvy
Customer Focus

Safety:   a strong commitment to ensure all people are provided with a safe, healthy and respectful environment.

Industry Competitive Benefits:   Medical, Dental, Vision and Employee Assistance Programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:   In House & Online Learning & Development, as well as an Education Assistance Program.
Quality:   a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.
Other Perks:   Free Bag of Premium Pet Food each month, Free Parking and more!
What are you waiting for? Join the pack!
Come as you are.
We value diversity in all forms and know the power it can bring. Workplace equality allows for creative ideas to bloom, diverse points of views to be heard, and increases overall happiness. That sounds pretty good to us.

title: SRM Promo Effectiveness Manager
description:
Job Description:
Title : SRM Promo Effectiveness Manager
Location: Chicago, IL
Workstyle : Onsite
Mars does not sponsor visas for this role. This position is eligible for relocation benefits
The SRM Promo Effectiveness Manager (this role) reports to the SRM Director of Trade & Promo serving as a key business co-pilot for Sales and as an integral member of the local center of excellence team for trade investment. This role helps deliver profitable category & profit pool growth with customers, partnering with Sales, CBU and Revenue, Strategy & Operations teams to evaluate and optimize the portfolio of trade investment decisions. This includes Marketing team co-pilot support to ensure trade investment productivity for Mars Snacking and our customers are in line with portfolio and CBU/Brand strategies and align with enterprise SRM principles and business objectives. The Primary objectives for the SRM Promo Effectiveness Manager are to:
Provide input for the creation of Compelling Trade Promotional Strategies. Develop appropriate Brand Trade promotional strategies with clear and compelling execution plans with recommended promotional calendars. This includes the creation, maintenance and continuous improvement of TP information, analyses and case studies to support SRM, Sales and CBU Marketing teams.
Maximize category growth opportunities achieved through trade promotional investments. Serve as a strategic thought partner to Channel Trade Managers by providing SRM insights, evaluating trade investment opportunities, and recommending actions that improve revenue, margin, and ROI for the CBU/Brands you support.
Improve Trade ROI Capabilities and trade promotional investment productivity across the organization.  Partner closely with Sales & Customer Marketing teams to analyze customer and national trade promotional events, using insights to drive greater accuracy and robustness of promotional forecasting and a deeper understanding of key TPE metrics/concepts (Trade ROI, Trade Leverage & ‘3 Star’ Promotions). This includes providing expert support to KAM teams, ensuring TPM tools/solutions are appropriately used for fact based decision support as part of pre and post event analysis.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Support Sales Leadership team, SRM Director of Trade and Promo and KAMs to deliver the annual growth requirements in line with trade promotional budgets by conducting customer event level ROI analysis and utilizing insights gathered to inform ongoing customer promotional plans.
Under the guidance of the SRM Director of Trade and Promo, support improved management, transparency and ROI productivity of TP investments by:
Partnering with KAM/KA Analysts to strengthen the depth and breadth of pre and post event trade promotion evaluations.  This includes providing guidance to Sales for accurate & timely event volume & financial information within TPM systems/tools to ensure proper funds management, ROI analysis and demand planning
Monitoring compliance to promotional guidelines at account or budget holder level
Supporting KAMs and Sales budget holders to verify & consolidate TP event level exceptions versus guidelines through S&OP+ process
Own the creation and analysis of all trade promotional reporting for the CBU/brands and Channels/customers, including on a periodic basis:
Monitoring Retail Promotional Landscape across CBUs/brands (e.g. Promotional Price Points)
Conducting detailed promotional analysis across channels/pack types to highlight opportunities
Tracking competitors & multi-category promotional pricing and changes in strategy
Work with Sales, CMI and CBU Marketing to create quarterly trade promotional reporting, highlighting progress against business targets in trade leverage, trade shape and 3* promotions.
Own the creation and maintenance of the CBU/ brand trade promotional learning library to ensure a clear understanding of the categories' promotional dynamics, including internal and external information, by:
Partnering with CMI and CBU/Marketing teams to ensure category and consumer trade promotional norms are incorporated into activity plans & NPD execution.
Performing regular post evaluations of national trade promotional programs, to inform learnings and ongoing strategies.
Regularly assessing the results of competitor strategies, both within and outside the categories to help inform growth opportunities.
Support the SRM Trade ROI lead and Demand S&F in evaluating and creating recommendations on long term portfolio trade promotional strategy for the market by creating robust fact bases on brand/pack/channel/competitor dynamics.
What are we looking for?
5-8 years experience in a FMCG/consumer products organization with an analytical background.
A proven record in analyzing and modelling complicated data sets and the creation of analysis tools (Excel, Databases) to aid decision making. The ability to use this information to reach insightful conclusions and create robust recommendations (‘So What’) and present outputs in an informative way.
An understanding of the commercial P&L from RRP to NSV is required, including how changes in sales and investments affect this.
Functional/technical understanding and know-how specifically:
Trade Promotional Knowledge (Preferred) – An understanding of the concepts of trade promotions (Price discounts, uplifts, base & incremental volumes, trigger funding), ROI, TLI, Trade shape would be helpful. As would the ability to calculate customer trade margin through different investment levels.
Trade Promotional Systems/Tools (Preferred)  - Knowledge and experience using analytical models and TPM/PEA tools for accurate promotional scenario planning & analysis, including the integration with other information management/forecasting systems (e.g., Funds Management and Demand Planning)
Trade Promotional Strategy (Helpful) – demonstrated understanding of the strategic & operational impacts of trade promotional decisions across the 5C’s (i.e. Category, Consumer, Customer, Competitor, Company) and the impact of changes on the value chain.
Able to build successful working relationships, being a key contributor as part of a cross functional team.
Able to effectively articulate and convey ideas and thoughts in a simple and effective manner. Not afraid to voice ideas or opinions within a peer group.

Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.

Strategic mindset with significant experience developing and executing strategic frameworks

Job Description:
The Business Partner, Value Creation is a key member of the Integration Management Office (IMO) Value Creation team, reporting to the Value Creation Lead. The Spend Better program is a critical pillar of the global Synergy program, focused on unlocking sustainable cost savings and productivity across the end-to-end value chain. Spend Better encompasses a broad range of value-creation opportunities, with an elevated emphasis on Directs (Direct Materials, Packaging, Recipe & Formulation, and Design-to-Value) alongside manufacturing productivity, network optimization, logistics efficiency, travel and overhead optimization, and other structural cost-reduction initiatives.
We are looking for a highly commercially oriented Finance Business Partner to partner the global Spend Better program and drive greater rigor, pace and intensity in delivering value. This role will operate at the intersection of Finance, Procurement, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Marketing and other functional teams. The successful candidate will work with senior stakeholders globally while partnering closely with Finance Business Partners across regions and functions.
The role requires someone who can identify opportunities, challenge assumptions, translate operational opportunities into financial value, and ensure that savings are both delivered and sustained.
What are we looking for?
10+ years of progressive Finance experience, ideally with significant experience in cost transformation, productivity, value creation or performance improvement.
Demonstrated experience across the Directs ecosystem— encompassing direct materials procurement finance, raw & packaging materials, R&D/formulation optimization, Design-to-Value (DtV), and Bill of Materials (BOM) cost architecture.
Substantial background in Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Food & Beverage, or FMCG manufacturing environments where recipe, packaging, and factory conversion are central to cost structures.
Demonstrated experience translating operational productivity opportunities into validated, sustainable financial savings, with a strong understanding of manufacturing cost drivers and the ability to distinguish structural savings from volume, mix, inflation, FX and other financial effects.
Experience operating in large, complex, multinational organizations is strongly preferred.
Technical / Commercial Capability:
End-to-End Directs & Manufacturing Economics: Strong grasp of recipe costing, ingredient functionality trade-offs, packaging specifications, yield/scrap dynamics, and conversion economics.
Cost Engineering & DtV Acumen: Familiarity with teardowns, Design-to-Value principles, clean-sheet pricing, and supplier margin analysis.
Financial Modeling & Valuation: High proficiency in complex business cases, discounted cash flows, switchover investment paybacks, and synergy stage-gate tracking.
Financial Control & Accounting: Deep understanding of COGS, standard costing variance (purchase price variance, usage variance), P&L flow-through, and inventory valuation.
Analytical Precision: Ability to distill massive datasets across ERP systems and bill of materials into clear financial drivers and actionable business decisions.
Leadership & Behavioral Capabilities:
Commercial & Technical Co-Pilot: Operates with a growth and value-creation mindset; understands the operational levers behind the numbers.
Constructive Challenger: Confident in probing assumptions made by both procurement buyers and technical developers to ensure targets are robust.
Navigating Ambiguity: Thrives in dynamic, fast-paced integration environments, balancing strategic vision with granular operational execution.
Influencing Without Authority: Exceptional interpersonal skills to mobilize cross-functional global partners who do not report directly to this position.
Clarity of Communication: Exceptional storytelling and synthesis skills, simplifying technical and financial complexities for senior executive audiences.
What will be your key responsibilities?
1. Drive the Global Spend Better Agenda:
Act as the primary Finance Business Partner to the global Spend Better program.
Partner with the Spend Better team to translate overall synergy ambition into actionable, prioritized portfolio of initiatives across both commercial directs (e.g., strategic sourcing, supplier terms, clean-sheet costing) and technical/operational directs (e.g., recipe reformulations, ingredient harmonization, specification optimization, lightweighting, and scrap/yield improvement).
Drive urgency, accountability and transparency across the global program.
Challenge the organization to identify additional opportunities and accelerate delivery.
Establish a consistent global approach to identifying, quantifying and tracking value creation.
2. Identify, Evaluate and Quantify Value Creation Opportunities:
Partner with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, R&D, Procurement, Marketing and other functions to identify cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
Assess opportunities through a rigorous financial and operational lens, including cost drivers, baseline economics, implementation requirements and risks.
Translate operational initiatives such as formulation changes, packaging redesign, manufacturing productivity, logistics optimization and Design-to-Value into measurable financial outcomes.
Champion Design-to-Value (DtV) and total cost of ownership (TCO) frameworks, converting technical and operational proposals into verified financial value.
Rigorously stress test business cases to ensure that reported savings represent true economic value rather than timing, volume, mix or accounting effects.
Help teams prioritize initiatives based on value, feasibility, speed and sustainability.
3. Establish Savings Rigor and Governance:
Define and embed robust methodologies for establishing baselines, calculating savings and measuring financial impact.
Create clear distinction between identified, validated, implemented and realized savings.
Ensure initiatives are appropriately reflected in financial forecasts and actual results.
Partner with regional and functional Finance teams to reconcile initiative-level savings to P&L and other financial measures.
Identify gaps between operational savings claims and financial outcomes and drive resolution.
Establish mechanisms to prevent double counting and ensure clear ownership of benefits.
4. Performance Management and Executive Visibility:
Develop a fact-based view of Spend Better performance across regions, functions and initiatives.
Build dashboards and management routines that highlight delivery versus ambition, risks, opportunities and required interventions.
Provide insightful analysis to senior leadership and governance forums.
Surface emerging risks early and work with initiative owners to develop recovery plans.
Prepare high-quality financial and business insights for SteerCo and other senior leadership discussions.

Work closely with Finance Business Partners across regions and functions, ensuring alignment between global program governance and local execution.
Build strong relationships with senior stakeholders across Supply Chain, Procurement, R&D, Manufacturing, Marketing and Finance.
Influence without direct authority and drive consistency across a highly matrixed organization.
Share best practices and replicate successful value-creation initiatives across markets and categories.

title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
Overview
We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer who lives and breathes Azure Cosmos DB and knows how it is implemented underneath. Your mission is to make throttling disappear from Microsoft's AI plugin registry with fast, surgical, high-ROI changes. Success is objective: throttling goes away, reliability goes up, and latency goes down, even as scale grows. You will see the results in days, not quarters.
We are the Agent Tools and Lifecycle team in Microsoft's Copilot, Agents and Platform (CAP) organization. We build the service behind the AI plugin registry. Admins use it in the Microsoft 365 admin center to govern the plugins (skills, connectors, and agents) that extend Microsoft Copilot, and users discover and use those plugins across products such as Copilot Chat, Cowork, Teams, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. The registry is a core part of Microsoft's AI architecture, alongside Work IQ, and Copilot experiences across Microsoft depend on it. If you use an AI solution from Microsoft, you likely are working with our service. Come join us at the center of AI transformation at Microsoft!
As a hands-on individual contributor, you will be the technical leader for the AI plugin registry's Azure Cosmos DB tier. Our catalog of plugins and agents, and the entitlements and policies that decide who can use them, live in Cosmos DB in data centers worldwide, including sovereign clouds. Traffic keeps growing as the registry expands to experiences such as Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, and Microsoft Foundry. Experience working on the internals of Cosmos DB or a comparable database, such as MongoDB, Amazon DynamoDB, or Apache Cassandra, and an understanding of the hardware and network limits that make them throttle, are especially valuable. Our global reach means 24/7 on-call service.
This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Cut request unit (RU) consumption to make throttling go away, fast. Start with the queries that use the most RUs, where we see room for 50–90% reductions: turn cross-partition and fan-out queries into point reads from Cosmos DB or Azure Blob Storage, batched reads, or single-partition queries, and tune indexes.
Pick work by return on investment. Ship several targeted fixes in parallel, each within days, and measure each one in production. Take on a larger redesign only when the data shows smaller fixes cannot get there, and deliver it in steps that each pay off.
Fix hot partitions and size limits at the source: partition keys, document design, indexing policies, and API contracts that give high-traffic calls the keys they need for point reads. When data has to move, migrate it with zero downtime across all environments, including sovereign clouds.
Decide what belongs in Cosmos DB. Move large, binary, unbounded, or rarely queried content to Azure Blob Storage or other storage, weighing latency, availability, and data-residency needs.
Remove redundant and sequential database calls on our busiest paths with batching, request coalescing, and caching, and use retry budgets, load shedding, and graceful degradation so database pressure does not turn into failed requests.
Work with product management and the teams that call us to give each caller a throttling budget. Find callers that request the same unchanged data again and again, help them cache on their side, and lower the budgets of the heaviest callers over time.
Make success measurable: own the telemetry, dashboards, and alerts, RU use per API and per caller, partition skew, availability, and latency. Set targets, show the effect of every change, and spot limits before we hit them.
Raise the bar through AI: write AI skills that review designs and code for Cosmos DB mistakes, find high-RU queries, and show engineers how to fix them, so your expertise scales across the team. Use agentic tools to build and validate fixes faster, following Responsible AI practices. Mentor engineers and represent us with the Azure Cosmos DB product group.
Serve as a Designated Responsible Individual (DRI) in our 24/7 on-call rotation, lead data-tier incident response, and turn what we learn into lasting fixes.

At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower scientists to solve some of the world's biggest problems by developing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology.
The Microsoft Quantum team is dedicated to developing the first scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer. Our work spans quantum hardware, error correction, and integration with Azure. Our accomplished, diverse international team is focused on building a scalable quantum computing system. Our full-stack strategy encompasses breakthroughs in quantum device physics, scalable readout, and control infrastructure powered by cryoelectronics. As quantum computing enters a pivotal phase of accelerated growth, this position offers an opportunity to contribute to a transformative technology.
Microsoft is seeking a Quantum Technical Program Manager (TPM), at the Senior to Principal level , to lead the end-to-end delivery of next-generation quantum hardware systems. You will drive cross-functional execution across research, engineering, and external partners to develop scalable, production-ready quantum solutions. Working closely with subsystem research and development leaders in areas such as control, packaging, and test and measurement, you will align roadmaps, manage risks, and deliver critical milestones. This high-impact leadership role calls for deep technical expertise, strong program management skills, and a customer-focused mindset.
You will collaborate with physicists, quantum theorists, experimentalists, research and systems engineers, technical program managers, supply chain experts, cloud architects, and external partners to accelerate the scale-up of topological qubits and quantum systems. If you thrive on complex program challenges, can navigate ambiguity, and are passionate about foundational technologies, we invite you to help shape the future of quantum computing.
At Microsoft, our mission—to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more—guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. Join CCS and help us accelerate AI transformation for our customers and the world.
The Service Portfolio and Delivery organization, part of CCS, is leading the effort to enable customer success on the Microsoft Cloud by harnessing leading, AI-powered capabilities and human expertise to deliver innovative solutions that accelerate business value, drive operational excellence, and nurture long-term loyalty. One of the key mechanisms through which Microsoft activates the incredible talent of its technical teams for customer success is Microsoft Unified. Unified enables a proactive approach with customers that accelerates value creation and sustains growth for the Microsoft Cloud. It serves as a growth engine for the company by getting hands-on with customers to understand their priorities and help drive adoption and optimization at speed.
The Unified Foundational Offers team creates and brings to market commercial offerings that provide expert guidance and problem resolution, ensuring customers get value and success from their Microsoft technologies.
Role overview
Lead the portfolio operating layer for Foundational Offers across enterprise and mission-critical services. This is a senior services and support business leadership role, bringing horizontal accountability to a portfolio that spans embedded AI guidance through premium engineering partnership. You will connect portfolio economics, pricing, delivery capacity, engineering priorities and investment returns so that leaders can make coherent decisions across the full support and services ladder.
Working as a peer to offer program leaders, you will establish shared operating models and turn competing business needs into defensible portfolio choices. Success is measured by decisions changed: pricing revised to protect differentiated customer value, engineering priorities sharpened and capacity assumptions corrected before funding. You will enable stronger revenue and margin quality, retention, value realization and upgrade movement through influence and business judgment, rather than acting as a sole quota owner or a coordination-only program manager.

title: BIM Designer & Coordinator
description:
About the Team

Industrial Compute is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. Working alongside our capital partners, engineering teams, and construction organizations, we design and deliver large-scale, mission-critical compute campuses that power the next generation of AI. Our Design organization brings together engineering, construction, and digital design to ensure facilities are coordinated, constructible, and optimized from the earliest planning phases through deployment.

About the Role

We are seeking a BIM Designer & Coordinator to support the planning and design of large-scale industrial and mission-critical facilities. In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain multidisciplinary BIM models across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural disciplines, enabling early design validation, constructability reviews, equipment planning, and cross-functional coordination.

You will partner closely with internal engineering teams, external design consultants, contractors, and project stakeholders to produce coordinated BIM deliverables that improve design quality, reduce project risk, and support efficient execution across Industrial Compute's global infrastructure portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

 - Develop and maintain conceptual and schematic BIM models for large-scale industrial and MEP-intensive facilities.

 - Coordinate BIM models across Civil, Architectural, and Structural disciplines.

 - Create and maintain federated models used for design reviews, spatial coordination, constructability analysis, and clash detection.

 - Model major building systems including equipment layouts, utility corridors, electrical rooms, mechanical rooms, structural framing, site infrastructure, and architectural constraints.

 - Coordinate equipment clearances, maintenance access, routing zones, shafts, risers, utility entrances, and major MEP pathways.

 - Translate engineering sketches, basis-of-design documents, equipment lists, one-line diagrams, and planning documentation into coordinated BIM models.

 - Support early design activities including test-fit studies, routing evaluations, phasing plans, utility coordination, and design option analysis.

 - Maintain BIM standards including model organization, file naming conventions, worksets, shared coordinates, view templates, and model health.

 - Support multidisciplinary coordination using Navisworks, Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Revizto, or similar collaboration platforms.

 - Prepare model views, coordination packages, exports, and documentation for design reviews and stakeholder meetings.

 - Support model-based quantity takeoffs, equipment tracking, asset information, room data, and design progress reporting.

 - Review consultant and contractor BIM deliverables for quality, coordination, completeness, and compliance with project BIM standards.

 - Help maintain digital design assets that support planning, design development, construction coordination, and operational handoff.

Discipline Focus Areas



CIVIL BIM DESIGNER

title: Data Scientist, Cloud Distribution & Growth
description:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

 - Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Industrial Compute organization develops and delivers the large-scale power, data center, and compute infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team works across energy, electrical, mechanical, controls, site development, construction, commissioning, operations, and external partners to turn demanding campus power requirements into safe, reliable, and executable solutions.

About the Role

We are seeking a Design Engineer, Power Generation to develop and integrate power-generation systems for large-scale AI infrastructure campuses. You will translate campus load, reliability, schedule, and operating requirements into practical generation architectures and technical design criteria, supporting both behind-the-meter generation and hybrid grid-and-generation strategies.

This is an individual contributor role with broad technical ownership from early concept and technology evaluation through detailed design, equipment selection, construction support, commissioning, and performance validation. You will work with internal engineering teams, utilities, OEMs, EPC partners, developers, and operators to resolve interfaces, make disciplined tradeoffs, and establish repeatable power-generation designs that can scale across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop power-generation concepts, reference architectures, design criteria, and site-specific requirements based on campus demand, phasing, reliability targets, grid availability, fuel strategy, site constraints, and operating objectives.

 - Evaluate generation technologies and system configurations, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, battery energy storage, microgrids, black-start systems, and hybrid grid-connected solutions.

 - Define and review plant electrical and mechanical balance-of-plant requirements, protection and controls philosophy, grid-paralleling and islanding behavior, redundancy, maintainability, and operational modes.

 - Translate AI infrastructure load profiles and deployment schedules into generation capacity plans, equipment sizing, ramp strategies, performance requirements, and commissioning criteria.

 - Lead technical diligence of OEM, EPC, developer, and supplier proposals; review calculations, one-line diagrams, layouts, specifications, studies, schedules, and design assumptions to identify gaps and material risks.

 - Coordinate interfaces across utility interconnection, substations, campus electrical distribution, cooling systems, controls, fuel supply, emissions, water, civil design, permitting, construction, and operations.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs across availability, efficiency, emissions, cost, schedule, constructibility, scalability, maintainability, and long-term operating flexibility, and document clear technical recommendations.

 - Support equipment selection, procurement, design reviews, factory and site acceptance testing, construction issue resolution, commissioning, performance testing, and operational handoff.

 - Investigate design or field-performance issues, drive corrective actions with partners, and incorporate lessons learned into engineering standards, specifications, and future reference designs.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation or industrial power systems, including responsibility for generation facility design or integration.

 - A bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience taking generation projects from concept and equipment selection through detailed design, with direct involvement in procurement, construction support, commissioning, or performance testing.

 - Strong understanding of generation technologies such as gas turbines or reciprocating engines and their supporting electrical, mechanical, and fuel systems, including protection, controls, grid paralleling, islanding, and black start.

 - Ability to evaluate engineering studies, drawings, specifications, and supplier proposals; identify technical risks; and make defensible tradeoffs among safety, reliability, cost, schedule, and maintainability.

 - Experience resolving design interfaces across engineering disciplines and coordinating equipment suppliers, engineering and construction partners, utilities, and operators.

 - Sound judgment around safety, reliability, constructibility, maintainability, and technical risk, with the ability to make decisions when requirements or information are incomplete.

 - Ability to document design requirements, assumptions, and decisions clearly and explain technical recommendations to engineering, delivery, commercial, and leadership teams.

 - Professional Engineer licensure and experience developing reusable engineering standards and reference designs across multiple projects.

 - Hands-on experience deploying and commissioning onsite generation for campuses or industrial facilities with demand in the hundreds of megawatts or more, including large load steps and rapid power fluctuations.

 - Experience co-designing and deploying battery energy storage systems (BESS) with onsite generation, including power and energy sizing, controls integration, load smoothing, and frequency support.

 - Familiarity with utility interconnection studies, emissions and environmental constraints, fuel-supply requirements, and generation permitting.

 - Experience validating generation and storage performance through dynamic studies and field testing, including load steps, load rejection, generator trips, and transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Equipment
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories. You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL).

You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment. You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement

 - Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness. Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers.

 - Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

 - Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations. Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements.

 - Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers. Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register. Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it.

Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

 - Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI’s engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams.

 - Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format. Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes.

 - Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits.

 - Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history.

 - Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed.

Factory Witness Testing (FWT)

 - Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team. Agree on requirements before testing begins.

 - Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants.

 - Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation. Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier.

Deviation Management

 - Assess short shipments and missing or failed tests in partnership with Manufacturing Operations.

 - Coordinate supplier support to resolve issues at the project site.

 - Document each deviation and track the agreed actions through closure.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and project management.

 - Experience coordinating FAT and FWT with suppliers and resolving equipment quality issues.

 - Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality. Experience managing controlled documents and deviations.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - PMP or equivalent project management certification.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.

As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.

In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.

You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow.

We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments.

 - Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity.

 - Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures.

 - Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution.

 - Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning.

 - Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks.

 - Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows.

 - Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone.

 - Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain the reliability and availability of critical network infrastructure.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Have hands-on experience deploying, activating, and troubleshooting WAN circuits with telecommunications carriers, fiber providers, or cloud service providers.

 - Have a strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including optical networking, Ethernet, TCP/IP, BGP, and Layer 2/3 connectivity.

 - Are comfortable debugging network issues across multiple layers, from physical fiber connectivity and optical errors to routing and traffic forwarding.

 - Have experience working with data center networking, carrier infrastructure, cloud interconnects, or large-scale WAN environments.

 - Understand physical network infrastructure concepts such as fiber cabling, port mappings, optical distribution frames, and network equipment connectivity.

 - Can independently investigate ambiguous connectivity problems, isolate root causes, and work across internal and external teams to restore service.

 - Have experience with scripting or automation tools and are motivated to reduce manual work through repeatable, scalable processes.

 - Enjoy working directly with infrastructure and take pride in owning technical problems from initial deployment through operational resolution.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment where infrastructure requirements evolve rapidly and engineering decisions have a direct impact on global scale.

Nice to Have

 - Experience building or operating large-scale backbone networks, hyperscale data center networks, or cloud provider interconnect infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with optical transport technologies, network telemetry, and advanced troubleshooting of physical network links.

 - Experience automating network operations using Python, Go, or infrastructure automation frameworks.

 - Experience deploying new network PoPs or supporting large-scale network expansion projects.

 - Experience collaborating with carriers, colocation providers, and cloud networking teams on complex connectivity deployments.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI's ability to advance AI research and deliver products at global scale depends on reliable, high-performance infrastructure.

As a member of the Global Network Infrastructure team, you will help build the connectivity foundation supporting some of the world's most demanding compute environments. Your work will directly contribute to expanding OpenAI's global network footprint, bringing critical infrastructure online, and ensuring the reliability of the systems powering frontier AI.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

 - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

 - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

 - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

Hardware Procurement Operations enables OpenAI’s hardware and infrastructure businesses to execute supplier engagements and purchases at speed while maintaining financial discipline, clear ownership, and effective controls.

You will own procurement execution for complex infrastructure deals, including land transactions, lease agreements, power purchase agreements, and fast-moving colocation and fiber engagements. This senior individual contributor role combines hands-on lifecycle management with commercial judgment and building scalable operations. You will recognize gaps in proposed supplier engagements, work with business owners, sourcing, Legal, and Finance to improve them, and translate agreements into executable purchasing and payment plans. You will also build standard processes and automation that help teams move faster while reducing deal risk.

In this role, you will:

description:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

Our analysts and investigators make sense of complex data to understand emerging risks and investigate severe misuse. They work closely with engineers who build tools that extend what human experts can see and do. The design of the investigative workflow shapes how effectively people can use those tools and act on what they learn.

About the Role

We’re hiring a service designer to shape how investigative cases move through OpenAI, from the first signal through review and action. You’ll work alongside investigators to understand what each case requires and how the overall workflow shapes what investigators can accomplish.

You’ll bring that perspective to the people who shape investigative operations and the engineers who build the underlying systems. Together, you’ll decide where a change would help and see how it works in real cases.

In this role, you will

 - Work alongside investigators to understand how cases move across teams and systems. Consider what that process means for people at risk, people whose activity is under review, and the people responsible for acting on a finding.

 - Lead the cross-team work of mapping investigative workflows, designing improvements with the people who use and operate them, and putting agreed changes into practice.

 - Guide engineering decisions about how investigative systems fit together to support the overall workflow.

title: Software Engineer, Traffic Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.

Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.

You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.

This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.

 - Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.

 - Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.

 - Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.

 - Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.

 - Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.

 - Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.

 - Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.

description:
