About the role
District Managers serve as the engine driving our revenue strategy. However, administrative and tactical tasks—such as gathering pipeline updates, managing escalations, and assembling QSR materials—frequently detract from their primary focus. The Sales Operations Business Partner directly addresses this challenge by assuming ownership of these functions.
Operating within a designated group of districts across the AMER Enterprise or Commercial segment, you will collaborate closely with District Managers to drive operational workflow, maintain data integrity, and interface with key partners across Deal Desk, Finance, Legal, Channel, and SEs among other teams. By streamlining operational tasks, you enable DMs to dedicate more focus to team coaching and deal execution. While forecast ownership and team leadership remain with the DM, your mandate is to deliver precise, timely, and fully managed support across underlying Sales processes.
This role is a trusted business partner position requiring strong analytical abilities, business partnering, and strong communication skills. It serves as a key pillar for operational execution in Sales Operations. As you partner with leadership, optimize district workflows, and manage cross-departmental coordination, the role offers a path toward Sales Operations Manager and Senior Sales Operations Manager positions—bringing expanded scope, increased strategic influence, and elevated partnership with senior sales leadership.
What you will do
Pipeline hygiene. Track pipeline quality in Salesforce and Clari across your districts. Follow up with AEs to update and clean opportunities, and flag hygiene gaps to the DM.
Forecast preparation. Pull district data ahead of weekly forecast calls, flag anomalies and changes, and prepare the roll-up the DM reviews.
Escalation triage. Take in customer and internal escalations, route them to the right team, and track each one to resolution so the DM is not the default inbox.
Deal Desk coordination. As required, follow up on Deal Desk requests and communicate approval status back to the DM and AE.
POC and expedite tracking. Monitor POC and expedite requests, keep stakeholders updated, and coordinate logistics across teams.
QSR preparation. Pull District data and build pre-work for Quarterly Sales Reviews, then track post-meeting action items to closure.
Annual planning support. Support territory and district data analysis, capacity modeling, and annual planning preparation.
Cross-functional coordination. Act as the district’s day-to-day contact for Finance, Legal, Channel, Marketing, and SE teams on operational requests.
Requests and cadence. Handle reporting requests and operational asks from DMs, and keep a working cadence (a weekly sync with each DM plus forecast call support).
How this role fits
You will work alongside the Regional Sales Operations team, which owns region-wide consistency, governance, and leadership reporting. Your focus is narrower and deeper: the day-to-day operations of your assigned districts. Forecast commits, deal strategy, AE coaching, and executive customer relationships stay with the District Manager.
What success looks like in your first six months
Your DMs report more time spent coaching AEs and less time on operational work.
Deal Desk and escalation cycle times in your districts get faster.
Pipeline hygiene in your districts improves and forecast calls start from clean data.
QSR prep takes your DMs noticeably less time, while delivering higher value insights.
What you bring
5+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Finance, or another analytical, business-facing role.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Working knowledge of Salesforce; experience with Clari or a similar forecasting tool is a plus.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara’s Machine Learning, AI, Analytics & Data (MAAD) team builds the intelligence and technology that helps our go-to-market teams work faster, make better decisions, and spend more time with customers.
As the Director, GTM AI Engineering you’ll run our AI Engineering team for GTM. You’ll work closely with Data Science, Analytics, and Data Engineering to serve Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, and GTM leadership. This is a hands-on Director role. Expect to spend about 70% of your time building (prototyping agents, writing code, designing evals) and about 30% leading the team, setting strategy, and influencing stakeholders.
You’ll build intelligent workflow experiences. That ranges from AI agents and copilots that take manual work off sellers’ plates, to signals for propensity and prioritization, to the data, evaluation, and measurement foundations that make these products reliable and trusted.
The ideal candidate is AI-native. You already run your own work through agents every day, you’ve shipped AI products to production, and you get as excited about a seller’s first “wow, this saved me an hour” moment as you do about a clean architecture.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.
In this role, you will:
Build hands-on. Prototype, ship, and iterate on AI agents, copilots, and workflow automations for GTM teams, from the first demo to a production system people rely on.
Build the platform, not just the apps. Own the architecture of the shared GTM AI platform: orchestration, LLM and tool gateways, identity and access, and the MCP and SDK contracts that let the GTM web app, Salesforce, Slack, desktop, and Claude plugins share one set of governed capabilities.
Make evals a first-class discipline. Design evaluation frameworks for agent and LLM behavior, including golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, human review loops, and regression suites, and run them in development and production. Use transcript analysis and eval results to find failures, guide what to fix first, and show quality improving over time.
Lead with AI day to day. Use agents, coding assistants, and agent harnesses in your own daily work, and build the shared tooling, patterns, and harnesses that make the whole team faster.
Stay ahead of the curve. Track new models, agent frameworks, MCP and tool ecosystems, and context engineering, and turn them into practical recommendations for Samsara's GTM use cases: what to adopt, what to test, and what to ignore. Make clear build-versus-buy calls on vendor tools, not just models.
Drive adoption with the field. Be the go-to advocate for AI across Sales, CS, and Support. Run demos, earn credibility with reps and frontline managers, collect real feedback, and turn skeptics into power users.
Set the strategy. Own the technical and product strategy for GTM AI, including the data foundations, instrumentation, governance, and observability these products depend on. Decide which prototypes move onto the shared platform, which merge, and which retire. Own model routing across vendors and the per-user spend controls that keep AI cost in line with value. Influence senior leaders on AI priorities, investment, and the operating model.
Ship revenue-critical intelligence. Own the forecasting, propensity, and CRM data-quality work that sales leadership acts on, and keep it calibrated, validated, and clear about its limits. Be comfortable across data and analytics engineering, and act as a business leader when the work calls for it.
Partner across GTM, Product, and Engineering. Work with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, Operations, Product, and Engineering leaders to find high-value opportunities, define success metrics, and turn them into durable products.
Build for trust. Put a pragmatic responsible-AI approach in place: safety, privacy, reliability, and human-in-the-loop workflows with clear approval and escalation paths. Agents that act on CRM and customer data run with per-user, least-privilege permissions, and changes to systems of record get human approval first.
Automatically included
All Roles : Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
People Manager Roles : Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing AI Engineering team
Minimum requirements for the role:
10+ years across software engineering, machine learning, data science, or data platforms, including meaningful leadership experience. You still write code regularly.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience.
Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM applications and agentic workflows to production, including tool use, retrieval, context engineering, and production reliability.
Production full-stack and cloud engineering experience (for example Python or TypeScript, AWS, and Databricks), including owning systems that other teams depend on.
Demonstrated experience designing and running evaluation frameworks for LLM or agent systems, and using them to drive quality decisions.
Daily, fluent use of AI agents and coding assistants in your own work, and a point of view on how they change the way teams build.
A track record of shipping internal or customer-facing AI/ML products with measurable business impact.
Experience with predictive modeling, experimentation, analytics, and data engineering foundations.
Strong product judgment and the ability to turn ambiguous business problems into simple, valuable solutions.
Excellent communication with both executives and frontline users. You can demo to a sales floor and present to a VP on the same day.
A people-first leadership style with a track record of hiring, developing, and keeping strong technical talent.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience building AI or decisioning products for Sales, Customer Success, Support, Marketing, or other GTM functions, ideally in a fast-growing enterprise SaaS environment.
Experience with CRM, customer data, support, and knowledge-management systems (such as Salesforce, Gong, Gainsight, Zendesk, and Databricks), and connecting agents to them (for example, through MCP servers or similar integrations).
Experience with agent SDKs and harnesses (such as Claude Code / Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or similar) and LLM observability tooling, eval tooling such as Braintrust or MLflow, and model APIs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
Experience operating AI products at scale, including cost management, monitoring, and governance.
A visible habit of learning in public, such as writing, talks, open-source work, or internal “what’s new in AI” sessions.

location: Remote - Austin; Remote - Seattle; San Francisco, CA, United States

As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About this role:
Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and help choose the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Build the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. Your designs, reviews, and instincts help raise the ceiling for the whole team. You will help shape how Samsara works, keep a high bar, be intellectually honest, work with urgency and deliver iteratively, as we scale globally and across new offices.
What you bring
2+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , on products that shipped to real customers and then had to survive in the field.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have helped bring up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping poorly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
Embedded Linux on the gateway side - Yocto or Buildroot, kernel drivers, device trees.
CAN and J1939 work on commercial vehicles , including reverse-engineering data bus parameters across makes and models.
Python and Bash for tooling , and hardware-in-the-loop test automation.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

title: Internal Purchasing Specialist
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.

About the role

You're the front door for everything Standard Bots buys to build, test, and demo physical robots: prototype parts, test fixtures, shop tools, pilot and trade-show builds. Engineers and customer-facing teams count on you to get what they need fast, and you'll keep the controls tight while you do it. And you won't do it by hand forever: you'll build AI-assisted workflows so routine requests move with almost no manual touch.

📍 Location

This is a full-time, remote role open to candidates in the US. You'll sit on the Finance team, report to the Accounting Manager, and work closely with teams across the company.

What you'll do

- Run the internal purchasing queue end to end: intake, clarify specs, source, buy, track delivery, and close out.

- Respond to every request within one business day and turn standard purchases around the same day.

- Triage urgent R&D and customer POC needs so engineering work never sits blocked waiting on a purchase.

- Keep requesters posted on status, ETAs, and substitutions, so nobody has to chase you.

- Find the right vendor on price, lead time, and quality, and get quotes on larger purchases.

- Set up and maintain vendors in Ramp, including W-9s, payment terms, and vendor ownership.

- Build a preferred-vendor list and negotiate pricing or accounts with high-volume suppliers.

- Issue POs, confirm receipt, and act as vendor owner and first invoice reviewer. The Accounting Manager is the second approver.

- Enforce the purchasing policy and approval thresholds, and route exceptions to the right budget owner.

- Tag every purchase with the correct GL account, department, and project, so R&D, POC, and capex costs are clean at month-end.

- Flag fixed-asset purchases to the Accounting Manager with the details needed for capitalization and asset tagging.

- Keep records audit-ready, with approvals, quotes, receipts, and invoices tied to each PO.

- Roll out the move from open Ramp card spend to centralized purchasing: communicate the change, train teams, and manage the transition.

- Report monthly on spend by department, category, and vendor, plus cycle time and open requests.

- Spot recurring purchases and convert them into standing orders, catalogs, or blanket POs.

What you'll bring

- 3+ years in purchasing, procurement, or purchasing-focused operations, ideally at a hardware, robotics, or manufacturing company.

- Hands-on experience with a spend management platform (Ramp, Brex, Coupa, or similar) and PO-based purchasing.

- Working knowledge of basic accounting concepts: GL coding, capex vs. opex, accruals, and three-way match.

- Ai Automation - this role scales through automation, not headcount. You’ll build AI agents to run intake, vendor comparisons, POs, invoice matching, and status updates, document every workflow so others can run it, and keep pushing up the share of requests that close with no manual touch.

- A service mindset: you're fast, responsive, and comfortable juggling many small requests at once.

- Strong judgment on when to follow policy and when to escalate.

Nice to have

- Experience standing up a purchasing function or rolling out a new spend policy.

- Exposure to audit-ready controls and fixed-asset tracking.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $70,000 - $85,000 depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Mechanical Engineer (On-site)
description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

At Standard Bots, we're revolutionizing real-world automation by making robotic systems accessible to everyone. Our AI-powered platform enables robots to tackle unprecedented challenges through an intuitive instruction interface, bringing the power of software automation to physical spaces.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

We're building Bolt, a mobile manipulation platform: an autonomous mobile base carrying our robot arms. We're hiring two Mechanical Engineers to join the Bolt team early in their careers and grow with the product. One will work on the upper body — the structures, mounts, and covers that carry the arms, sensors, and payload on the base. One will support the electrical team and proof-of-concept builds — brackets, enclosures, harness routing, test fixtures, and the quick-turn parts that keep prototypes moving. You'll design in SolidWorks, build what you design, and test it on real robots.


📍 LOCATION

This is an on-site role based at our new Boston-area office, where Bolt is designed, built, and tested, with some flexibility on days in the office once you're up to speed. You'll work next to the build area, electronics lab, and test floor. Relocation assistance is available.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design parts and assemblies in SolidWorks — sheet metal, machined parts, 3D prints, and off-the-shelf hardware — and release drawings with correct tolerances and callouts

 - Build and test prototypes: order parts, assemble, instrument, run tests, and document results

 - Do first-pass engineering analysis (loads, stress, deflection, fastener sizing) and know when to ask for a deeper look

 - Support cross-functional builds with EE, software, and test — fixtures, mounts, cable routing, quick fixes on the floor

 - Keep BOMs, drawings, and PDM records accurate through fast design iterations

 - Learn the product deeply: assemble robots, tear them down, and find out what breaks


WHO YOU ARE

You're early in your career, you've built real hardware (robotics team, FSAE, rocketry, research lab, internships, or a first job), and you want to work on robots you can watch move. You'd rather be in the shop than in a meeting, you ask good questions, and you finish what you start. On-site presence matters here: the fastest way to learn this job is standing next to the robot.


SKILLS YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related, and 0–3 years of hands-on hardware experience (internships and project teams count)

 - Fundamentals: Solid grasp of statics, strength of materials, materials selection, and GD&T basics

 - Tool Fluency: Proficient in SolidWorks parts, assemblies, and drawings; comfortable with a 3D printer, basic machine tools, and hand tools

 - Hands-on: You've assembled, tested, and debugged something physical and can show it

 - Clarity of Communication: You write clear test notes and design summaries and ask for help early

 - Growth + Optimism: Excited by new domains and challenges, and eager to pick up new context fast

 - Excelling in Ambitious Environments: You thrive in a fast-moving team with changing requirements and tight timelines


BONUS POINTS FOR

 - Robotics, AMR/AGV, or vehicle project experience

 - Basic electrical skills — reading schematics, wiring, crimping, soldering

 - Python or scripting for test data

 - Sheet metal and machining DFM exposure


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The base salary range for this role is $95,000 to $125,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

At Standard Bots, we're revolutionizing real-world automation by making robotic systems accessible to everyone. Our AI-powered platform enables robots to tackle unprecedented challenges through an intuitive instruction interface, bringing the power of software automation to physical spaces.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

We're building Bolt, a mobile manipulation platform: an autonomous mobile base carrying our robot arms. We're hiring two Senior Electrical Engineers for its electronics. One will focus on the safety system — the safety controller, dual-channel I/O, e-stop and safety-rated power cutoff, safety scanners and encoders, and the evidence that gets it certified. One will focus on upper/lower integration — the electrical architecture that joins arms, base, and control box: harnessing, connectors, communication buses, and the boards that bridge them. Both take designs from concept through production release and work hands-on in the lab and on the robot.


📍 LOCATION

This is an on-site role based at our new Boston-area office, where Bolt is designed, built, and tested, with some flexibility on days in the office once you're up to speed. On-site you'll have a fully equipped electronics lab, a test floor, and production robots steps from your desk.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the design and validation of PCBAs and electrical subsystems in your focus area from concept through production release

 - Safety focus: design the safety architecture with Functional Safety — safety PLC or safety controller, dual-channel inputs and outputs, STO and safe power cutoff, safety laser scanners, safety-rated encoders — and produce the design evidence for ISO 13849 PL d / Cat 3 certification

 - Integration focus: own the system electrical architecture — harness and connector design, bus topology (EtherCAT, CAN), power and signal distribution between arms, base, and control box — and lead bring-up of integrated prototypes

 - Do the hands-on, technically deep work: schematic capture, PCB layout, board bring-up, test plans, and root-cause debugging

 - Lead design reviews, contribute to the component library and release process, and be a technical contact for PCB and harness vendors

 - Mentor associate and mid-level engineers


WHO YOU ARE

We don't require a background in robotics — but we do require deep, hands-on electronics experience. We find most success with engineers from industrial automation, machinery safety, automotive, or aerospace who want to apply that depth to robots they can watch move. Our ideal candidate expects to spend roughly 60% of their time on design and 40% on lab, integration, and manufacturing support.


SKILLS YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience: Bachelor's or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering (or related) and 5+ years designing, building, and testing PCBAs and electrical systems, including designs you've taken through production release

 - EE Depth: Strong in digital electronics (MCUs, Ethernet, SPI/I2C/UART), analog and sensing, power sequencing and protection, and system-level grounding and EMC

 - Focus Depth: Either safety-rated design (ISO 13849 / IEC 62061 / IEC 61508 — redundant architectures, diagnostics, STO, safety fieldbus) or system integration (harness and connector design, bus topology, bring-up of multi-board systems)

 - Tool Fluency: Proficient in Altium Designer for schematic capture and multi-layer layout; harness tooling (Altium Harness, Rapid Harness, or similar) a plus

 - Debugging Mastery: Scope, logic/protocol analyzer, and bench instruments; you document what you find and converge on a fix quickly

 - Clarity of Communication: Clear design documentation, crisp trade studies, and design reviews that make your peers better

 - Impact Driven: A reliable, manufacturable board that ships beats an elegant one that never leaves the lab

 - Excelling in Ambitious Environments: You thrive in a fast-moving team with changing requirements and tight timelines


BONUS POINTS FOR

 - Mobile robot safety: ISO 3691-4 / ANSI R15.08, safety laser scanners, safe speed and field switching

 - AMR navigation and localization hardware: lidar and camera integration, IMU and wheel odometry, RTK-GNSS, indoor RTLS (UWB or similar)

 - Real-time industrial fieldbuses (EtherCAT, CAN/CANopen, EtherNet/IP, CIP Safety / FSoE)

 - Motor control and encoder interfaces; battery and high-current power distribution

 - EMC/EMI design and compliance testing (CE/UL, IEC 61000 series)

 - Taking products from prototype through NPI to volume manufacturing


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $195,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

 - Debugging Mastery: Scope, current probe, thermal camera, and bench instruments; you document what you find and converge on a fix quickly

 - Clarity of Communication: Clear design documentation, crisp trade studies, and design reviews that make your peers better

 - Impact Driven: A reliable, manufacturable robot that ships beats an elegant one that never leaves the lab

For many of them, public transit isn't a convenience. It's how they get to a job, a hospital, or a classroom.
Checklists are where public-sector software starts. They shouldn't be where it stops. The real test is whether a dispatcher can fix a missed pickup in seconds, or whether a rider with a disability can book a trip without a phone call. Our users span paratransit eligibility managers, call center agents, dispatchers, and agency leaders, plus the riders, caregivers, and students on the other end. Each one deserves a product that's insights-first, obvious to use, and delightful, especially the communities with the fewest alternatives.

You'll also drive how design itself can be AI-led, moving from static mockups to rapid prototypes to production-ready code, working side by side with engineers. This isn't AI for AI's sake. Make every workflow insights-first, so data surfaces the right decision at the right moment instead of sitting in a report.

title: Staff Systems Engineer, Simulation Systems Verification and Validation Lead
description:
Zoox is on an ambitious journey to develop a full-stack autonomous mobility solution for cities. Simulation lets us test our driving software against far more scenarios than we can drive on public roads. For simulation results to count toward our safety case, we must show how closely the simulator matches reality and how much uncertainty the remaining difference adds to our safety metrics. We are seeking a Simulation Systems Verification and Validation (Sim VnV) Lead to own that work across the full autonomy stack. You will define how to validate simulation at the sensor, perception, planning, and full-pipeline levels, lead the cross-functional program that executes the sim VnV program, and turn the results into clear evidence about when and where simulated miles can support safety clearance decisions. You will work closely with simulation, perception, planning, hardware, safety, data science, and systems engineering teams. This is a highly visible, technical leadership role on the critical path to safely scaling our service. The ideal candidate demonstrates systems thinking, can lead a complex program across teams, and knows how to validate a model of a closed-loop system that has an AI controller inside it. In this role, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end simulation V&V strategy across different levels of integration ranging from sensors-only through the full system behavior for the purpose of constructing a safety case for fully autonomous driving on public roads.

  • Define the data sets, metrics, and comparison methods.

  • Lead a recurring cross-functional sim validation program with simulation, perception, planning, systems engineering, safety, and data infrastructure teams. Set milestones and cadence, track risks and dependencies, and drive decisions to closure.

  • Partner with statisticians and data scientists on estimators that combine simulated and real-world results into safety performance measures.

  • Write the methodology documents and validation reports, and present results, risks, and recommendations to engineering and executive leadership.

  • Mentor engineers across teams in V&V practice and systems thinking.

    • Qualifications

  • M.S. or higher in Systems, Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, or Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in verification and validation of safety-critical systems that contain software or autonomy (for example autonomous vehicles, ADAS, aerospace guidance and flight software, or robotics).

  • A record of leading technical programs across several teams, from an ambiguous problem statement to a delivered result.

  • Working-level experience validating a simulation or model against real-world data so that its results could support a decision, preferably for a closed-loop system with software or a learned controller in the loop.

Lead Production Technician
ROLE SYNOPSIS:
The Lead Production Technician is a field-based technical leader who supports the Production Foreman by converting priorities into safe, reliable, and efficient field execution. This role serves as the primary technical resource and escalation point for Production Technicians and drives production uptime, troubleshooting, asset stewardship, and operational discipline across an assigned area.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Own the day-to-day technical quality of field operations within the assigned area and ensure Production Technicians execute safely and consistently.
Serve as the primary technical resource and escalation point for Production Technicians.
Support startups, shutdowns, troubleshooting, and abnormal operations, providing on-site or remote technical support to resolve issues and stabilize production.
Escalate unresolved risks and issues to the Production Foreman with clear problem definition, field context, and a recommended path forward.
Train and mentor Production Technicians on proper use of PI Vision, CygNet, Ranger, and Power BI to identify deferring wells, trend production performance, and manage deferment priorities.
Review high-volume pads daily, monitor high-touch wells, and initiate corrective actions to support stable production.
Monitor gathering-system performance, alarms, and well behavior and coordinate actions on constraints.
Use PI Vision, CygNet, and Power BI to identify abnormal trends, underperformers, and downtime events before they escalate.
Evaluate high-spend project performance, including gas lift conversions, ESP installations, and base-well tie-ins.
Coordinate production recovery during midstream outages, weather events, and other high-impact or unplanned disruptions.
Manage deferment using Power BI tools, Code Manager, PI Vision, CygNet, and Ranger to maintain accurate production-loss tracking and prioritize the highest-impact items.
Partner with the Optimization team on deferment, well issues, and troubleshooting to drive production uplift and resolve chronic problems.
Align daily priorities with the Production Foreman and coordinate technicians, contractors, Maintenance, Automation, and Engineering resources.
Track work to completion, communicate remaining risks or open items, and use Ranger to direct technician efforts toward the highest-impact priorities.
Identify nesting opportunities to consolidate work, reduce mobilization costs, and improve field efficiency across technician routes.
Improve problem definition and maintenance-notification quality, support repairs, and verify issue resolution.
Identify repeat failures and collaborate with Production Engineering, Facilities Engineering, Artificial Lift Engineering, Automation, and Reliability teams on chronic equipment issues and active projects.
Lead by example in hazard recognition, safety observations, stop-work authority, and operational discipline.
Support SORAs, JSAs, permits, safeguard verification, pre-job meetings, housekeeping, and procedural compliance.
Hold safety conversations and complete safety observations during each rotation; ensure HSE compliance among field vendors and contractors.
Ensure technician routes are current on OOOOA inspections, site inspections, plunger inspections, and managed-valve registry requirements; address gaps and overdue items.
Validate well-coding accuracy for Normal Ops, Base Backout, and Engineering/Optimization and ensure technicians update coding daily to reflect real-time field conditions.
Confirm technician verifications are meaningful and identify non-repetitive gaps.
Lead operational handover of new pads from Commissioning to Production Operations and review performance, failures, and outstanding issues before acceptance.
Coordinate with Development to document events in Enbase from initial startup and perform initial operation and optimization following handover.
Participate in MOC reviews, PSSR walkdowns, PHAs, HAZOPs, and 30% design reviews.
Coordinate contractors and vendors in alignment with Operations priorities and verify work completion and safety compliance.
Coach Production Technicians, share lessons learned, maintain operating notes and shift handovers, and review technician night notes for completeness and repeat issues.

Submit all travel and expense reports accurately and on time.

High school diploma or equivalent required.

Experience utilizing data and available resources to solve operational problems.

Experience using data to drive operational decisions.
Knowledge of databases, data architecture, and technologies used to transport and transform data.

Growth mindset with the ability to learn quickly and adapt to changing conditions.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
High aptitude and interest in new technology.
Collaborative team player who builds effective partnerships across functions.
Naturally inquisitive and proactive approach to problem solving.
Excellent listening, interpersonal, and communication skills.
Change-oriented mindset focused on improving processes and outcomes.
Ability to manage changing priorities, delays, and unexpected events.
Strong ownership, accountability, and initiative.

Physical demands include frequent standing, walking, bending, stooping, pushing, pulling, climbing, and repetitive movements involving the hands, arms, shoulders, legs, and torso. bp is committed to investing in lower carbon energy so we can meet our ambition to reach net zero by 2050. And while we’re still mostly in oil and gas today, bioenergy is one of our five transition growth engines and a key focus to help us support the global energy transition.

The team operates around 50 sites in 32 states with a robust development pipeline.
About the role
The Operations Technician is responsible for the overall safe operation, maintenance, and performance of a landfill gas to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) processing facility.  This position requires 25%-50% travel per month (First 12 months in the position will require 50% travel per month when hired for a new plant. Travel requirement will reduce to 25% per month when working at an existing plant or in year 2 and beyond for a new plant).
Key accountabilities
Manage the safe operation of the plant during assigned shift in the most efficient and productive method to maintain compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s) and prescribed safety and environmental standards.
Make periodic inspections of plant equipment to determine proper and normal operating conditions. Check and record operational data such as fluid levels, temperatures and pressures, compare to trends and have the ability to make corrections as needed.
Review daily operating reports and other records to ensure specified operating characteristics in control of the plant equipment.
Perform preventive maintenance and troubleshooting on plant instrumentation and equipment.
Detect and correct faulty and malfunctioning mechanical and electrical components, devices and equipment.
Operate advanced instrumentation and process control systems.
Diagnose equipment malfunctions during emergencies and direct activities to restore normal operation or to shut down malfunctioning unit.
Test electrical systems and continuity of circuits in electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures using testing devices such as ohmmeters and voltmeters.
Troubleshoot and repair electrical system wiring from control wiring up to 480 volts. Install, remove and modify equipment.
Notify Lead Operation Technician and Regional Manager of shutdown or major changes in power output of unit.
Maintain all plant equipment and structures in accordance with manufactures and Aria Energy guidelines.
Maintain a clean work space including the plant building, control room, rest room, break room and grounds.
Write routine reports and correspondence.
Maintain daily operation logs for shift in accordance with prescribed standards.
Assist in planning maintenance and outage activities.

Responds in a timely manner to callouts and work overtime as required

Intermediate Electrical, Chemical and Mechanical experience.

Understanding of process control systems as applied to landfill gas collection and processing.
Technical / Troubleshooting skills with ability to read and understand complex technical manuals and schematics.

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables.
Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
Proficient using computers (experience using MS Word, Excel and email systems) and monitoring equipment to measure, record and make adjustments within operating parameters, perform fault finding and repair as well as required scheduled maintenance.

title: Planner/Scheduler
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:
Job Family Group:
Operations Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
The Planner / Scheduler plans and schedules maintenance, instrumentation and electrical (I&E), brownfield construction, and greenfield construction work across Permian production operations. The role helps develop field-ready work packages, integrates resource and material requirements, manages the work-order backlog, and builds realistic weekly and monthly schedules that support safe, efficient execution.
Reporting to the Construction & Maintenance Manager, this position serves as the central coordination point among Operations, Maintenance, I&E, Construction, Reliability, Engineering, Supply Chain, warehouse personnel, contractor resources, and our Midstream partners. The Planner / Scheduler identifies constraints and conflicts before work reaches the field, aligns work with operating and shutdown windows, and helps minimize production impacts and avoidable schedule disruption.
Success requires proficiency in SAP as the work management system, disciplined use of the work-management process and supporting systems, strong field engagement, practical knowledge of maintenance and construction execution, and the ability to turn competing priorities into a clear, executable plan. The role owns planning quality, schedule readiness, backlog visibility, schedule-performance reporting, and continuous improvement through feedback from execution teams.
Key Accountabilities
Work planning and job readiness
Develop detailed work packages that define scope, work steps, labor, materials, tools, equipment, permits, isolations, safety requirements, access needs, and completion criteria.
Perform field walkdowns with Operations and execution teams to validate scope, identify constraints, and confirm site readiness before work is committed to the schedule.
Estimate job durations and resource requirements using historical performance, job complexity, and crew capability.
Confirm materials, rentals, contractor support, and long-lead items are identified, ordered, tracked, staged, and available before mobilization.
Integrated scheduling and coordination
Build and maintain integrated weekly and monthly schedules for Maintenance, I&E, construction, shutdown, turnaround, and commissioning activities.
Facilitate schedule-development and readiness meetings with team leads and partner functions; document priorities, owners, constraints, decisions, and schedule changes.
Balance workload across internal crews and contractors while identifying conflicts, capacity gaps, and competing resource demands early.
Coordinate work with Operations to align access, isolations, production impacts, outage windows, and return-to-service requirements.
Protect committed construction and maintenance milestones by communicating risks early and presenting practical recovery or resource options.
Backlog and work-management governance
Manage the work-order backlog through prioritization, aging, status review, scope validation, and escalation of work requiring leadership attention.
Maintain accurate work-order, equipment, PM, schedule, and completion data in the SAP and associated planning tools.
Coordinate timely closeout of completed work, including actual labor hours, materials used, execution feedback, and required documentation.
Promote adherence to the work-management process and continuously improve planning quality through feedback loops with field crews and team leads.
Performance, cost, and continuous improvement
Track and report schedule compliance, planning accuracy, planned-versus-unplanned work, backlog health, material readiness, carryover, break-in work, and work-order closeout performance.
Analyze maintenance and construction data to identify recurring constraints, productivity losses, cost drivers, and opportunities to improve PM strategies and execution efficiency.
Support cost transparency by aligning planned labor, contractor, equipment, and material requirements with approved work scopes and budgets.
Identify opportunities to combine work within common outage windows to reduce repeat mobilization, production deferral, and operational disruption.
Essential Experience and Education
High school diploma or equivalent.
Demonstrated experience planning or scheduling maintenance, construction, turnaround, or operations work in oil and gas, industrial, manufacturing, utilities, or a comparable asset-intensive environment.
Working knowledge of work-order planning, backlog management, preventive and corrective maintenance, job readiness, permitting, isolation, and contractor coordination.
Proficiency using SAP as a work management system to create and maintain work orders, support planning and scheduling, manage backlog visibility, and report on executable work plans.
Ability to perform field walkdowns and work effectively in an operating production environment.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to facilitate cross-functional planning meetings and communicate schedule risks, trade-offs, and decisions.
Desirable Criteria
Experience supporting upstream oil and gas production, wellsite facilities, gathering systems, or related Permian Basin operations.
Experience coordinating multi-discipline Maintenance, I&E, Construction, Reliability, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, warehouse, and contractor work.
Experience with shutdown, turnaround, tie-in, commissioning, and new-well facility scheduling.
Experience developing work packages, managing long-lead materials, and using schedule and backlog metrics to improve crew productivity.
